    /// Last value (V or A).
    pub stop: f64,
    /// Points including both ends. At least 2, or 1 when `start == stop`.
    pub num_points: usize,
}

impl DcSweepAxis {
    /// `num_points` values of `source_id` from `start` to `stop`.
    pub fn new(source_id: impl Into<String>, start: f64, stop: f64, num_points: usize) -> Self { … }

    /// SPICE's `.dc` form: from `start` in steps of `step` for as long as
    /// it doesn't pass `stop`. When `step` doesn't divide the span, the last
    /// value is short of `stop`, as in SPICE.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`SimError::InvalidComponent`] for a value that isn't finite, a step
    /// that is zero (with `start != stop`) or points away from `stop`, or
    /// more than 10⁷ points.
    pub fn from_step(
        source_id: impl Into<String>,
        start: f64,
        stop: f64,
        step: f64,
    ) -> Result<Self, SimError> { … }
}

/// Sweeps a voltage or current source across a range and solves the
/// operating point at each step.
///
/// Used for generating I-V curves and transfer characteristics. The returned
/// [`DcSweepResult`] has helpers to pull out plottable curves for any node
/// voltage or component current. Each point's Newton–Raphson starts from
/// the previous point's solution, as in SPICE, so a curve follows one
/// branch of a circuit with several operating points.
///
/// # Arguments
///
/// - `circuit` — the base circuit (unchanged; each sweep point gets a
///   modified copy)
/// - `source_id` — id of the [`VoltageSource`](CircuitElement::VoltageSource)
///   or [`CurrentSource`](CircuitElement::CurrentSource) to sweep
/// - `start`, `stop` — sweep endpoints (V or A), inclusive
/// - `num_points` — total points including both endpoints (minimum 2)
///
/// For two sources at once, as SPICE's `.dc V1 … V2 …`, see
/// [`dc_sweep_nested`].
///
/// # Errors
///
/// - [`SimError::InvalidComponent`] if `num_points < 2` or above 10⁷, `start` or `stop`
///   is not finite, or `source_id` doesn't match any voltage or current
///   source in the circuit
/// - Any [`SimError`] returned by [`solve_circuit`](crate::solve_circuit)
///   at one of the sweep points (propagated immediately)
///
/// # Example
///
/// ```
/// use sindr::{Circuit, CircuitElement, dc_sweep};
///
/// let circuit = Circuit {
///     ground_node: "0".into(),
///     components: vec![
///         CircuitElement::VoltageSource {
///             id: "V1".into(),
///             nodes: ["n1".into(), "0".into()],
///             voltage: 0.0,
///             waveform: None,
///         },
///         CircuitElement::Resistor {
///             id: "R1".into(),
///             nodes: ["n1".into(), "0".into()],
///             resistance: 1_000.0,
///         },
///     ],
///     ..Default::default()
/// };
///
/// // Sweep V1 from 0 V to 10 V in 11 steps.
/// let sweep = dc_sweep(&circuit, "V1", 0.0, 10.0, 11).unwrap();
/// assert_eq!(sweep.points.len(), 11);
///
/// // I = V/R should rise linearly from 0 to 10 mA.
/// let curve = sweep.component_current_curve("R1");
/// assert!((curve.last().unwrap().1 - 0.010).abs() < 1e-9);
/// ```
pub fn dc_sweep(
    circuit: &Circuit,
    source_id: &str,
    start: f64,
    stop: f64,
    num_points: usize,
) -> Result<DcSweepResult, SimError> { … }

/// A two-source DC sweep: one [`DcSweepResult`] along the inner source per
/// value of the outer one.
pub struct NestedDcSweepResult {
    /// Component id of the outer (slower) source.
    pub outer_source_id: String,
    /// One curve per outer value, in sweep order.
    pub curves: Vec<NestedDcSweepCurve>,
}

/// One curve of a [`NestedDcSweepResult`]: the inner sweep at one value of
/// the outer source.
pub struct NestedDcSweepCurve {
    /// The outer source's value for this curve (V or A).
    pub outer_value: f64,
    /// The inner sweep at that value.
    pub sweep: DcSweepResult,
}

/// Sweeps two sources, `inner` fastest: for each value of `outer`, a full
/// sweep of `inner`. SPICE's `.dc SRC1 … SRC2 …`, with `SRC1` as `inner`.
/// This is how a family of device curves is drawn: a MOSFET's drain current
/// against V_DS for each V_GS, or a BJT's collector current against V_CE
/// for each base current.
///
/// Each point's Newton–Raphson starts from its neighbour along the inner
/// axis, and each curve's first point from the first point of the curve
/// before.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// [`SimError::InvalidComponent`] for an axis with fewer than 2 points (1 is
/// allowed when its `start` and `stop` are equal), values that aren't
/// finite, a source that isn't a voltage or current source in the circuit,
/// both axes on the same source, or more than 10⁷ points in all; and any
/// error from [`solve_circuit`](crate::solve_circuit) at a point.
///
/// # Example
///
/// ```
/// use sindr::{dc_sweep_nested, Circuit, CircuitElement};
/// use sindr::dc_sweep::DcSweepAxis;
///
/// // Two sources into a 1 kΩ: the current is (V1 + V2) / 1 kΩ.
/// let circuit = Circuit::new(
///     "0",
///     vec![
///         CircuitElement::VoltageSource {
///             id: "V1".into(),
///             nodes: ["a".into(), "b".into()],
///             voltage: 0.0,
///             waveform: None,
///         },
///         CircuitElement::VoltageSource {
///             id: "V2".into(),
///             nodes: ["b".into(), "0".into()],
///             voltage: 0.0,
///             waveform: None,
///         },
///         CircuitElement::Resistor {
///             id: "R1".into(),
///             nodes: ["a".into(), "0".into()],
///             resistance: 1e3,
///         },
///     ],
/// );
/// let sweep = dc_sweep_nested(
///     &circuit,
///     &DcSweepAxis::new("V1", 0.0, 1.0, 3),
///     &DcSweepAxis::new("V2", 0.0, 2.0, 2),
/// )
/// .unwrap();
/// assert_eq!(sweep.curves.len(), 2);
/// let last = sweep.curves[1].sweep.component_current_curve("R1");
/// assert!((last[2].1 - 3e-3).abs() < 1e-12); // (1 V + 2 V) / 1 kΩ
/// ```
pub fn dc_sweep_nested(
    circuit: &Circuit,
    inner: &DcSweepAxis,
    outer: &DcSweepAxis,
) -> Result<NestedDcSweepResult, SimError> { … }
```

## `sindr/src/error.rs`

Error type returned by the solver.

```rust
/// Anything that can go wrong while validating or solving a circuit.
///
/// Returned by [`solve_circuit`](crate::solve_circuit),
/// [`solve_transient`](crate::solve_transient),
/// [`solve_ac`](crate::ac_analysis::solve_ac), [`solve_tf`](crate::solve_tf),
/// [`solve_sensitivity`](crate::solve_sensitivity),
/// [`dc_sweep`](fn@crate::dc_sweep) and
/// [`temperature_sweep`](crate::temperature_sweep).
///
/// Variants split into four groups:
///
/// - **Design errors** ([`Design`](Self::Design)) — the hierarchy can't be
///   flattened.
/// - **Topology / validation errors** ([`NoGround`](Self::NoGround),
///   [`DisconnectedNodes`](Self::DisconnectedNodes),
///   [`FloatingNode`](Self::FloatingNode)) — caught before solving.
/// - **Numerical errors** ([`SingularMatrix`](Self::SingularMatrix),
///   [`InvalidSolution`](Self::InvalidSolution),
///   [`ConvergenceFailed`](Self::ConvergenceFailed)) — the matrix has no
///   unique solution or Newton–Raphson failed to converge.
/// - **Configuration errors** ([`InvalidComponent`](Self::InvalidComponent),
///   [`InvalidResistance`](Self::InvalidResistance)) — a component value or
///   analysis setting that the solver explicitly rejects.
pub enum SimError {
    /// The design hierarchy can't be flattened: an unknown block, a
    /// port-count mismatch, a recursive block or a repeated id.
    #[error("{0}")]
    Design(#[from] sindr_core::DesignError),

    /// No ground node was defined. Every circuit needs a reference node.
    #[error(
        "No ground node defined in circuit. Every circuit needs a ground (reference) node \
         — try connecting a component terminal to node \"0\"."
    )]
    NoGround,

    /// One or more nodes have no path to the rest of the circuit.
    #[error(
        "These nodes are not connected to the rest of the circuit: {0:?}. \
         Make sure every node has a path to ground through components."
    )]
    DisconnectedNodes(Vec<String>),

    /// A node has fewer than two component terminals attached and so can't
    /// carry current.
    #[error(
        "Node \"{0}\" has fewer than 2 connections and cannot carry current. \
         Connect it to at least 2 components."
    )]
    FloatingNode(String),

    /// The MNA matrix is singular — typically a voltage-source loop or a
    /// subcircuit that's not tied to ground.
    #[error(
        "Circuit matrix is singular — the circuit has no unique solution. \
         Common causes: voltage sources in a loop, or a subcircuit disconnected from ground."
    )]
    SingularMatrix,

    /// The solver produced NaN or infinity, usually due to component values
    /// spanning an extreme dynamic range.
    #[error(
        "Solver produced invalid values (NaN or Infinity). This usually means component \
         values span an extreme range. Try checking for very small or very large values."
    )]
    InvalidSolution,

    /// A component definition or analysis setting is malformed: a device
    /// `temperature` or BJT `bf` that isn't positive and finite, an id that
    /// names no suitable source or component, a non-finite or out-of-range
    /// sweep or transient setting, a transient of more than 10⁷ steps or a
    /// sweep of more than 10⁷ points, a bad initial condition. Carries a
    /// human-readable description naming the offending id or field.
    #[error("Invalid component: {0}")]
    InvalidComponent(String),

    /// A resistor's resistance is zero, negative or not finite.
    #[error(
        "Resistor \"{0}\" has a zero, negative or non-finite resistance, which is not physically meaningful."
    )]
    InvalidResistance(String),

    /// Newton–Raphson exhausted its iteration budget without converging,
    /// in DC after the gmin- and source-stepping fallbacks failed too.
    ///
    /// Carries the iteration count reached and the largest per-node voltage
    /// step `max_i |Vᵢ_new − Vᵢ_prev|` (V) at the final iteration. A step
    /// near the convergence tolerance suggests slow convergence — try
    /// scaling component values or supplying initial conditions. A large
    /// step usually means the circuit has no valid operating point (e.g. a
    /// nonlinear element with no DC path to ground).
    ///
    /// Note: this is the maximum *Newton step* between consecutive
    /// iterations, not a KCL residual `|F(x)|`.
    #[error(
        "Newton-Raphson failed to converge after {iterations} iterations \
         (max node-voltage step {max_step_volts:.3e} V). \
         The circuit may have no valid operating point."
    )]
    ConvergenceFailed {
        /// Number of Newton iterations executed before giving up.
        iterations: usize,
        /// Largest per-node Newton step on the final iteration (V): the max
        /// over node indices of `|V_new[i] − V_prev[i]|`.
        max_step_volts: f64,
    },

    /// Self-heating has no stable balance: a part's dissipation heats its
    /// junction, which raises its current, faster than its thermal path can
    /// carry the heat away. The real part would be destroyed.
    #[error(
        "thermal runaway in `{part}`: its junction passed {temperature:.0} K with no stable \
         operating point. Lower its dissipation, add emitter degeneration, or give it a \
         lower thermal resistance (heatsink)."
    )]
    ThermalRunaway {
        /// The part that ran away (the hottest one whose temperature feeds
        /// back into its model).
        part: String,
        /// Its junction temperature when the solve gave up (K).
        temperature: f64,
    },

    /// A [`Measurement`](crate::measure::Measurement) couldn't be taken on
    /// a result: an unknown node or component, a window outside the
    /// result, or a level the signal never crosses.
    #[error("measurement `{name}`: {reason}")]
    Measurement {
        /// The measurement's name.
        name: String,
        /// Why it couldn't be taken.
        reason: String,
    },
}
```

## `sindr/src/examples.rs`

Built-in example circuits.

Each circuit is exposed as a named function returning `Circuit` directly,
e.g. `sindr::examples::voltage_divider()`. The dynamic metadata-bearing list
(`get_examples()` returning `Vec<ExampleCircuit>`) is feature-gated behind
`examples` and intended for HTTP/UI consumers that need ids and descriptions.

```rust
/// Two resistors in series across a voltage source. Node `n2` shows the divided voltage.
pub fn voltage_divider() -> Circuit { … }

/// Two resistors in parallel. Current splits inversely proportional to resistance.
pub fn current_divider() -> Circuit { … }

/// Three resistors in series. Voltage drops proportional to resistance.
pub fn series_resistors() -> Circuit { … }

/// Current-limiting resistor protects an LED (modeled as a 2 V source).
pub fn led_circuit() -> Circuit { … }

/// 5 V source through a 1 A fuse and 100 Ω load. Toggle `blown` for the open-fuse case.
pub fn fuse_protection() -> Circuit { … }

/// Voltage source and current source in the same circuit, demonstrating superposition.
pub fn mixed_sources() -> Circuit { … }

/// Classic measurement bridge with four resistors. Bridge voltage is zero when balanced.
pub fn wheatstone_bridge() -> Circuit { … }

/// 5 V amplitude, 1 kHz sinusoidal source driving a 1 kΩ load.
pub fn sine_wave_source() -> Circuit { … }

/// First-order RC filter with -3 dB cutoff at ~159 Hz (R=1 kΩ, C=1 µF).
pub fn rc_lowpass_filter() -> Circuit { … }

/// 2:1 step-down transformer (L1=1 H, L2=0.25 H, k=0.999). 10 V primary → ~5 V on 100 Ω secondary.
pub fn transformer_stepdown() -> Circuit { … }

/// Classic NPN BJT amplifier. Base resistor sets bias, collector resistor sets gain.
pub fn npn_common_emitter() -> Circuit { … }

/// BJT driven into saturation to switch a load. Low base resistor ensures full turn-on.
pub fn npn_switch() -> Circuit { … }

    /// Returns all built-in example circuits with their display metadata.
    /// Order matches the difficulty grouping in the frontend.
    pub fn get_examples() -> Vec<ExampleCircuit> { … }

pub use meta::{get_examples, ExampleCircuit};
```

## `sindr/src/lib.rs`

A circuit simulator you embed in Rust: build a circuit as a typed value,
solve it natively or in WebAssembly, and get back numbers checked against
ngspice. Pure Rust, no C libraries, no global state. Besides voltages and
currents it answers design questions: whether each part stays inside its
ratings ([`check_ratings`]) and whether a spec passes ([`check_specs`]).
Accuracy against ngspice is tabled in the
[repository](https://github.com/steffendybvik/sindr-rs/blob/main/docs/ACCURACY.md).

`sindr` solves a [`Circuit`] — a list of components and a ground node —
and returns voltages, currents, and power for every component. The solver
picks the right path automatically:

- **Linear DC** — direct solve of the MNA system.
- **Nonlinear DC** — Newton–Raphson when diodes, BJTs, MOSFETs, etc. are present.
- **Transient** — Gear-2 (or trapezoidal or backward-Euler) timestepping
  when capacitors, inductors, or time-varying sources are present.
- **AC small-signal** — sinusoidal-steady-state via [`ac_analysis::solve_ac`].
- **Transfer function** — DC small-signal gain, input and output
  resistance (SPICE's `.tf`) via [`solve_tf`].
- **DC sensitivity** — derivative of an output with respect to each
  component parameter (SPICE's `.sens`) via [`solve_sensitivity`].
- **DC sweep** — operating point at each value of a swept voltage source,
  via [`fn@dc_sweep`].
- **Temperature sweep** — operating-point sweep over junction temperature
  via [`temperature_sweep`].

Device physics (diode, BJT, MOSFET, IGBT, JFET, varactor companion models)
live in the companion crate
[`sindr-devices`](https://crates.io/crates/sindr-devices). `sindr`
re-exports the few enums you'll typically need ([`BjtKind`],
[`MosfetKind`], [`JfetKind`], etc.).

### Quick start

How much current does a red LED draw from 5 V through 220 Ω?

```
use sindr::{solve_circuit, Circuit, CircuitElement};

let circuit = Circuit::new("gnd", vec![
    CircuitElement::VoltageSource { id: "V1".into(), nodes: ["vcc".into(), "gnd".into()], voltage: 5.0, waveform: None },
    CircuitElement::Resistor { id: "R1".into(), nodes: ["vcc".into(), "a".into()], resistance: 220.0 },
    CircuitElement::Led { id: "D1".into(), nodes: ["a".into(), "gnd".into()], color: "red".into(), temperature: 300.15 },
]);
let result = solve_circuit(&circuit)?;
let led = result.component_results.iter().find(|c| c.id == "D1").unwrap();
println!("{:.1} mA, {:.1} mW", led.current_through * 1e3, led.power * 1e3);

// About 1.8 V across the LED leaves about 3.2 V across R1.
assert!((led.current_through - 3.2 / 220.0).abs() < 1.5e-3);
```

### Data model and hierarchy

[`Circuit`] and everything in it comes from the [`sindr_core`] crate,
re-exported here as [`circuit`], [`design`] and [`waveform`]. Design tools
can depend on `sindr-core` alone. Besides its flat `components`, a
circuit can place [`Block`]s through [`Instance`]s, name `globals`, and
carry [`Part`] data (reference, symbol, footprint) the solver ignores.
Every analysis flattens the hierarchy first ([`Circuit::flatten`]: `X1.R1`,
`X1.mid`) and reports results under the flattened names. A broken
hierarchy is [`SimError::Design`].

### Capabilities

#### Analyses

| Analysis | Entry point | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Operating point (linear or nonlinear DC) | [`solve_circuit`] | Newton–Raphson for nonlinear devices |
| Transient | [`solve_transient`] | Gear-2 (default), trapezoidal or backward Euler ([`IntegrationMethod`]), steps up to the [`TransientConfig`]'s `tstep`, shortened by truncation-error control and landing on waveform breakpoints. [`solve_circuit`] also takes this path when the circuit has C, L or waveform sources, choosing 5 τ and τ/50 itself |
| AC small-signal | [`ac_analysis::solve_ac`] | Needs an [`ac_analysis::AcConfig`]. [`solve_circuit`] **never** runs AC |
| Transfer function (`.tf`) | [`solve_tf`] | DC small-signal gain, input and output resistance at the operating point. Input: a voltage or current source; output: a node voltage or a voltage source's current ([`TfOutput`]) |
| DC sensitivity (`.sens`) | [`solve_sensitivity`] | Adjoint method: d(output)/d(parameter) for resistances, source values, VCVS gain and VCCS gm. No device-model parameters, no AC sensitivity |
| Noise (`.noise`) | [`solve_noise`] | Thermal, shot and flicker noise at an output voltage, referred to an input source, with a per-source breakdown and band totals |
| DC sweep | [`fn@dc_sweep`], [`dc_sweep_nested`] | One voltage or current source, or two nested (`.dc V1 … V2 …`) |
| Temperature sweep | [`temperature_sweep`] | Re-solves the operating point at each junction temperature |
| Seeded operating point (`.nodeset`) | [`solve_circuit_with_initial_voltages`], [`ac_analysis::solve_ac_with_initial_voltages`], [`transfer_function::solve_tf_with_initial_voltages`], [`sensitivity::solve_sensitivity_with_initial_voltages`] | Seeds Newton for the DC, AC, `.tf` or `.sens` bias point |
| Self-heating | [`solve_circuit`], [`solve_transient`] | A part with [`Thermal`] data heats by its dissipation; DC iterates to a balance, transient carries a thermal RC. Results in `junction_temperatures`; no balance is [`SimError::ThermalRunaway`] |
| Ratings check | [`check_ratings`] | Each part against its absolute maximum [`Ratings`], at the operating point or every transient step. Missing ratings report unverified |
| Measurements and specs (`.meas`) | [`check_specs`] | [`Measurement`]s (value at x, min/max/avg/RMS, crossings, delay, rise/fall, settling, −3 dB) on any result; [`Spec`] limits give pass/fail and margin |
| Initial conditions (`.ic`, `UIC`) | [`TransientConfig::with_initial_voltages`], [`TransientConfig::with_initial_current`], [`TransientConfig::with_start`] | The state a transient starts from: switched on at t = 0 (default) or the DC operating point ([`TransientStart`]) |

Not available: distortion, pole-zero, AC sensitivity, Monte Carlo,
periodic steady state, S-parameters, variable-order integration.

#### Device models

| Device | Model |
|---|---|
| Diode, LED, Schottky, photodiode | Shockley; IS and V_T = kT/q follow each device's `temperature` (SPICE IS(T), XTI = 3) |
| Zener | A SPICE diode with breakdown `BV = vz` at 5 mA and RS = 1 Ω |
| BJT (NPN/PNP) | Ebers–Moll with Early voltage; not Gummel–Poon |
| MOSFET (NMOS/PMOS) | SPICE Level 1 (Shichman–Hodges), body tied to source, SPICE-signed VTO (negative for an enhancement PMOS); no BSIM |
| JFET (N/P) | Shichman–Hodges square law |
| IGBT | MOSFET-like gate control, square-law collector current |
| Varactor | Voltage-dependent junction capacitance (transient; AC at the bias point) |
| Op-amp | VCVS of gain 1e5, or with an [`OpAmpModel`]: single-pole GBW, slew rate, rail clamp, output resistance, offset, bias current |
| Comparator | VCVS of gain 1e5; no GBW or slew rate |
| Transformer | Linear coupled inductors |
| Battery | Open-circuit voltage by state of charge behind R0 and an optional R1‖C1; state of charge falls with charge drawn ([`battery::BatteryParams`]; Li-ion and CR2032 presets) |
| Voltage regulator | Piecewise linear: dropout, quiescent current, current limit, line and load regulation ([`RegulatorParams`]; LM7805 and AMS1117 presets) |

Parameters are Rust structs, not SPICE `.model` cards.

#### Convergence aids

Junction voltage limiting and Newton damping on every nonlinear solve,
with junctions starting at their critical voltage, as in SPICE. Newton
converges only once node voltages and every diode, LED and BJT junction
voltage have settled. When plain Newton–Raphson fails, the DC solve retries with gmin stepping
(1e-2 S down to 1e-12 S), then with source stepping (every source ramped
up from zero); [`SimulationResult::convergence_aid`] says which one was
needed. A transient step whose Newton solve fails is retried at half the
step.

#### SPICE input (feature `spice`)

[`spice`] reads a SPICE3 subset into a [`Circuit`]: R, L, C, V, I, D, Q
and X elements; `.subckt`, `.model`, `.param`, `.include`, `.lib`,
`.ic` and `.nodeset`; and the analysis cards `.op`, `.dc`, `.ac`, `.tf`,
`.sens` and `.tran`. Not supported: MOSFET (M)
and JFET (J) elements, controlled sources (E, F, G, H), coupled inductors
(K), `B` sources, most `.model` parameters (diodes always use IS = 1e-14,
N = 1; BJTs honour only BF), and netlist export.

The full list of what sindr doesn't do is in
[LIMITATIONS.md](https://github.com/steffendybvik/sindr-rs/blob/main/LIMITATIONS.md).

### Conventions

- **Ground node** must exist on at least one component. Its voltage is
  defined as 0 V — every other voltage is reported relative to it.
- **Node names** are arbitrary strings (`"0"`, `"gnd"`, `"vcc"`, …).
  Components share a node simply by referencing the same string.
- **SI units** throughout: V, A, Ω, F, H, s, K.
- **Sign conventions** are documented per [`CircuitElement`] variant.

### Cargo features

- `serde` *(default)* — `Serialize`/`Deserialize` impls on the public
  types.
- `examples` *(default, implies `serde`)* — exposes [`get_examples`] and
  the built-in named circuits (voltage divider, BJT amp, RC transient,
  etc.).
- `spice` — the SPICE3 netlist parser in [`spice`] (see below).

```toml
[dependencies]
sindr = "0.1.0-alpha.8"

# No serde, no built-in examples:
sindr = { version = "0.1.0-alpha.8", default-features = false }
```

### Transient results

A circuit with capacitors, inductors or waveform sources takes the
transient path, and [`SimulationResult::transient`] holds the time series.
[`solve_circuit`] picks the duration (5 τ) and step (τ/50) from the
circuit's time constants; to choose them, as SPICE's `.tran` does, call
[`solve_transient`] with a [`TransientConfig`].

```
use sindr::{Circuit, CircuitElement, solve_circuit};

// 5 V step into R = 1 kΩ, C = 1 µF: τ = 1 ms.
let circuit = Circuit {
    ground_node: "0".into(),
    components: vec![
        CircuitElement::VoltageSource {
            id: "V1".into(),
            nodes: ["in".into(), "0".into()],
            voltage: 5.0,
            waveform: None,
        },
        CircuitElement::Resistor {
            id: "R1".into(),
            nodes: ["in".into(), "out".into()],
            resistance: 1_000.0,
        },
        CircuitElement::Capacitor {
            id: "C1".into(),
            nodes: ["out".into(), "0".into()],
            capacitance: 1e-6,
        },
    ],
    ..Default::default()
};

let result = solve_circuit(&circuit).unwrap();
let tran = result.transient.expect("reactive circuit takes the transient path");

// The capacitor charges from 0 V towards 5 V.
let first = &tran.timesteps[0];
let last = tran.timesteps.last().unwrap();
assert!(first.node_voltages["out"] < 1.0);
assert!((last.node_voltages["out"] - 5.0).abs() < 0.1);
```

### SPICE netlist input

Parsing SPICE3 `.cir` decks into a [`Circuit`] lives behind the optional
`spice` feature (off by default, so the heavier parser dependencies stay
out of the baseline build):

```toml
[dependencies]
sindr = { version = "0.1.0-alpha.8", features = ["spice"] }
```

(`no_run`: it reads `amp.cir`, which doesn't exist where doctests run.)

```no_run
let netlist = sindr::spice::parse_file("amp.cir")?;
let result = sindr::solve_circuit(&netlist.circuit)?;
```

See the [`spice`] module for a runnable example, the supported subset and
strictness options.

### Where to look next

- [`Circuit`] / [`CircuitElement`] — the input format
- [`solve_circuit`] — the headline entry point
- [`SimulationResult`] — what you get back
- [`Waveform`] — time-varying source shapes
- [`SimError`] — what can go wrong

```rust
pub mod examples;

pub use examples::{get_examples, ExampleCircuit};

pub use sindr_core::design;

pub mod csv;

pub mod mna;

pub mod newton_raphson;

pub mod node_map;

pub mod noise;

pub mod ratings;

pub mod results;

pub mod sensitivity;

pub mod spice;

pub mod stamp;

pub mod temp_sweep;

pub mod transfer_function;

pub mod transient;

pub mod validation;

pub use sindr_core::waveform;

pub use circuit::{BjtModel, Circuit, CircuitElement, DiodeModel, OpAmpModel};

pub use dc_sweep::{dc_sweep, dc_sweep_nested, DcSweepResult, NestedDcSweepResult};

pub use design::{Block, DesignError, Instance, Part, Ratings, Thermal};

pub use error::SimError;

pub use measure::{check_specs, Measure, Measurement, Spec, SpecReport};

pub use mna::MnaSystem;

pub use node_map::NodeMap;

pub use noise::{solve_noise, NoiseConfig, NoiseResult};

pub use ratings::{check_ratings, RatingCheck, RatingKind, RatingStatus, RatingsReport};

pub use results:: { … }

pub use sensitivity::{solve_sensitivity, SensConfig, SensEntry, SensParameter, SensResult};

pub use temp_sweep::{temperature_sweep, TempSweepPoint, TempSweepResult};

pub use transfer_function::{solve_tf, TfConfig, TfOutput, TfResult};

pub use transient::{solve_transient, IntegrationMethod, TransientConfig, TransientStart};

pub use validation::validate_circuit;

pub use waveform::Waveform;

/// Battery equivalent circuits and presets, for [`CircuitElement::Battery`].
pub use sindr_devices::battery;

pub use sindr_devices::bjt::BjtKind;

pub use sindr_devices::igbt::IgbtParams;

pub use sindr_devices::jfet::JfetKind;

pub use sindr_devices::mosfet::MosfetKind;

/// Linear regulator parameters and presets, for [`CircuitElement::VoltageRegulator`]'s `model`.
pub use sindr_devices::regulator;

pub use sindr_devices::regulator::RegulatorParams;

pub use sindr_devices::varactor::VaractorParams;

/// Solves a circuit end-to-end and returns voltages, currents, and power for
/// every component.
///
/// The solver picks the analysis path automatically based on what the circuit
/// contains:
///
/// | Circuit contains | Path |
/// |---|---|
/// | Only resistors + sources | Linear DC (single matrix solve) |
/// | Diodes / BJTs / MOSFETs / etc. | Nonlinear DC (Newton–Raphson) |
/// | Capacitors / inductors / waveforms | Transient (Gear-2) |
/// | Reactive **and** nonlinear | Transient nonlinear |
///
/// For frequency-domain analysis, use [`ac_analysis::solve_ac`] directly.
/// For parameter sweeps, see [`fn@dc_sweep`] and [`temperature_sweep`].
///
/// # Errors
///
/// Returns [`SimError`] if the circuit fails validation (no ground node,
/// floating nodes, invalid component values, etc.) or if the solver itself
/// fails to converge or produces a singular matrix. See [`SimError`] for the
/// full list. A transient whose automatic span and step would take more than
/// 10⁷ steps is [`SimError::InvalidComponent`]; run it with
/// [`solve_transient`] and a coarser [`TransientConfig`].
///
/// # Example
///
/// ```
/// use sindr::{Circuit, CircuitElement, solve_circuit};
///
/// let circuit = Circuit {
///     ground_node: "0".into(),
///     components: vec![
///         CircuitElement::VoltageSource {
///             id: "V1".into(),
///             nodes: ["n1".into(), "0".into()],
///             voltage: 5.0,
///             waveform: None,
///         },
///         CircuitElement::Resistor {
///             id: "R1".into(),
///             nodes: ["n1".into(), "0".into()],
///             resistance: 1_000.0,
///         },
///     ],
///     ..Default::default()
/// };
///
/// let result = solve_circuit(&circuit).unwrap();
/// // I = V/R = 5 mA flowing through R1
/// let r1 = result.component_results.iter().find(|c| c.id == "R1").unwrap();
/// assert!((r1.current_through.abs() - 0.005).abs() < 1e-9);
/// ```
pub fn solve_circuit(circuit: &Circuit) -> Result<SimulationResult, SimError> { … }

/// Like [`solve_circuit`] but seeds the Newton–Raphson initial guess with
/// the supplied per-node voltages (V), keyed by node name. Equivalent to
/// SPICE's `.NODESET` directive — useful when a circuit has multiple
/// operating points (e.g. Schmitt triggers, latches) or when the default
/// heuristic fails to converge.
///
/// Only consulted when the circuit contains nonlinear elements; for purely
/// linear DC and for transient analysis the seed is ignored. Unknown node
/// names in `initial_voltages` are silently skipped.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// As [`solve_circuit`].
///
/// # Example
///
/// ```
/// use std::collections::HashMap;
/// use sindr::{Circuit, CircuitElement, solve_circuit_with_initial_voltages};
///
/// let circuit = Circuit {
///     ground_node: "0".into(),
///     components: vec![
///         CircuitElement::VoltageSource {
///             id: "V1".into(),
///             nodes: ["vcc".into(), "0".into()],
///             voltage: 5.0,
///             waveform: None,
///         },
///         CircuitElement::Resistor {
///             id: "R1".into(),
///             nodes: ["vcc".into(), "n1".into()],
///             resistance: 1_000.0,
///         },
///         CircuitElement::Diode {
///             id: "D1".into(),
///             nodes: ["n1".into(), "0".into()],
///             temperature: 300.15,
///             model: None,
///         },
///     ],
///     ..Default::default()
/// };
///
/// let mut nodeset = HashMap::new();
/// nodeset.insert("n1".to_string(), 0.7); // hint forward-bias diode drop
/// let result = solve_circuit_with_initial_voltages(&circuit, &nodeset).unwrap();
/// assert!(result.node_voltages["n1"] > 0.5);
/// ```
pub fn solve_circuit_with_initial_voltages(
    circuit: &Circuit,
    initial_voltages: &std::collections::HashMap<String, f64>,
) -> Result<SimulationResult, SimError> { … }
```

## `sindr/src/measure.rs`

Measurements and specs: a verdict on a result, and the reason when it
fails.

A [`Measurement`] turns a result into one number: the value at a time or
frequency, a min, max, average or RMS, a crossing time, a delay, a rise
or fall time, a settling time or a −3 dB point. A [`Spec`] adds limits to
a measurement, and [`check_specs`] reports, for each spec, the measured
value, its limits, pass or fail and the margin left. The ratings checks
([`check_ratings`](crate::check_ratings)) can ride along in the same
[`SpecReport`].

Measurements work on anything [`Measurable`]:

| Result | x axis |
|---|---|
| [`SimulationResult`] with a transient | time (s) |
| [`SimulationResult`] without one (DC operating point) | a single point at x = 0 |
| [`AcResult`] | frequency (Hz) |
| [`DcSweepResult`] | the swept source's value (V or A) |
| [`TempSweepResult`] | temperature (K) |

A [`Signal`] is a node voltage (`v(out)`), a voltage between two nodes
(`v(a, b)`) or a component's current (`i(R1)`, its
[`ComponentResult::current_through`](crate::ComponentResult::current_through)
direction). Its [`View`] picks the real value (the magnitude on an AC
result), dB (`20·log10|x|`) or phase in degrees (AC only, unwrapped
along the sweep).

SPICE `.meas` cards are parsed onto measurements by the `spice` feature
(`ParsedNetlist::measurements`).

```
use sindr::measure::{check_specs, Measure, Measurement, Signal, Spec, Stat};
use sindr::{solve_transient, Circuit, CircuitElement, TransientConfig};

// RC low-pass, τ = 1 ms, charging towards 5 V.
let circuit = Circuit::new(
    "0",
    vec![
        CircuitElement::VoltageSource { id: "V1".into(), nodes: ["in".into(), "0".into()], voltage: 5.0, waveform: None },
        CircuitElement::Resistor { id: "R1".into(), nodes: ["in".into(), "out".into()], resistance: 1e3 },
        CircuitElement::Capacitor { id: "C1".into(), nodes: ["out".into(), "0".into()], capacitance: 1e-6 },
    ],
);
let result = solve_transient(&circuit, &TransientConfig::new(10e-3, 10e-6))?;

let specs = [
    Spec::new(Measurement::new("vout_final", Measure::stat(Signal::v("out"), Stat::Final)))
        .between(4.9, 5.1),
    // 10–90 % rise of an RC is 2.2·τ.
    Spec::new(Measurement::new("rise", Measure::rise_time(Signal::v("out")))).at_most(2.5e-3),
];
let report = check_specs(&result, &specs);
assert!(report.passed(), "{report:?}");
let rise = report.checks[1].value.unwrap();
assert!((rise - 2.197e-3).abs() < 0.05e-3);
```

```rust
/// What a signal reads: a voltage or a current.
pub enum Quantity {
    /// Voltage at `node` (V), against `reference` or ground.
    Voltage {
        /// Node name.
        node: String,
        /// Reference node; `None` is ground.
        reference: Option<String>,
    },
    /// Current through a component (A), in the direction of its
    /// [`ComponentResult::current_through`](crate::ComponentResult::current_through).
    /// Falls back to [`SimulationResult::branch_currents`] for an element
    /// without a component result. Not available on AC results.
    Current {
        /// Component id, flattened (`X1.R3`).
        component: String,
    },
}

/// How a signal's value is read.
pub enum View {
    /// The value itself; the magnitude on an AC result.
    #[default]
    Value,
    /// `20·log10|x|`, in dB. On AC this is absolute (SPICE's `vdb`), not
    /// relative to the source amplitude.
    Db,
    /// Phase in degrees, AC only, unwrapped along the sweep so a phase that
    /// keeps falling past −180° reads −190°, not +170°.
    Phase,
}

/// A signal to measure: a [`Quantity`] read through a [`View`].
pub struct Signal {
    /// Voltage or current.
    pub quantity: Quantity,
    /// Value, dB or phase.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub view: View,
}

impl Signal {
    /// Voltage at `node` against ground: `v(node)`.
    pub fn v(node: impl Into<String>) -> Self { … }

    /// Voltage between two nodes, `node − reference`: `v(node, reference)`.
    pub fn v_diff(node: impl Into<String>, reference: impl Into<String>) -> Self { … }

    /// Current through a component: `i(component)`.
    pub fn i(component: impl Into<String>) -> Self { … }

    /// The same signal in dB.
    pub fn db(mut self) -> Self { … }

    /// The same signal's phase, in degrees (AC only).
    pub fn phase(mut self) -> Self { … }
}

/// A result a [`Measurement`] can be taken on.
pub trait Measurable {
    /// The signal's samples as `(x, y)` pairs, in ascending x.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// The reason it can't be read: an unknown node, a phase on a
    /// transient.
    fn trace(&self, signal: &Signal) -> Result<Vec<(f64, f64)>, String>;
}

/// A statistic over a signal, within the measurement's window.
pub enum Stat {
    /// Smallest sample.
    Min,
    /// Largest sample.
    Max,
    /// Mean over x, by trapezoids, so uneven time steps don't skew it.
    Avg,
    /// Root mean square over x, by trapezoids of y².
    Rms,
    /// Largest minus smallest sample.
    PeakToPeak,
    /// Integral over x, by trapezoids (V·s for a voltage on a transient).
    Integral,
    /// The last sample: the end of a transient, the only point of a DC
    /// operating point.
    Final,
}

/// Which way a signal crosses a level.
pub enum Edge {
    /// Going up through the level.
    Rise,
    /// Going down through the level.
    Fall,
    /// Either way.
    Cross,
}

/// Which crossing counts.
pub enum Occurrence {
    /// The nth one, from 1, in ascending x.
    Nth(usize),
    /// The last one.
    Last,
}

/// A signal crossing a level: SPICE's `WHEN v(out)=2.5 RISE=2`.
pub struct Crossing {
    /// The signal.
    pub signal: Signal,
    /// The level it crosses, in the signal's unit.
    pub level: f64,
    /// Rising, falling or either.
    pub edge: Edge,
    /// Which crossing.
    pub occurrence: Occurrence,
}

impl Crossing {
    /// The first crossing of `level`, either way.
    pub fn new(signal: Signal, level: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// Only rising crossings count.
    pub fn rising(mut self) -> Self { … }

    /// Only falling crossings count.
    pub fn falling(mut self) -> Self { … }

    /// The nth crossing, from 1.
    pub fn nth(mut self, n: usize) -> Self { … }

    /// The last crossing.
    pub fn last(mut self) -> Self { … }
}

/// What a [`Measurement`] measures. Each variant carries its own signal.
pub enum Measure {
    /// The signal's value at `at`, interpolated linearly: SPICE's
    /// `FIND v(out) AT=1m`.
    Find {
        /// The signal.
        signal: Signal,
        /// Where, on the result's x axis.
        at: f64,
    },
    /// A statistic over the window: SPICE's `AVG`, `RMS`, `MIN`, `MAX`,
    /// `PP` and `INTEG`.
    Stat {
        /// The signal.
        signal: Signal,
        /// Which statistic.
        stat: Stat,
    },
    /// The x at which a crossing happens: SPICE's `WHEN`.
    When(Crossing),
    /// `x(targ) − x(trig)`: SPICE's `TRIG … TARG …`, a propagation delay.
    Delay {
        /// Where the interval starts.
        trig: Crossing,
        /// Where it ends.
        targ: Crossing,
    },
    /// Rise or fall time between two fractions of the signal's swing over
    /// the window (0.1 and 0.9 for the usual 10–90 %). For a rise, from the
    /// last time it rose through `low` before it first rose through `high`;
    /// a fall the other way round.
    Transition {
        /// The signal.
        signal: Signal,
        /// [`Edge::Rise`] or [`Edge::Fall`].
        edge: Edge,
        /// Lower fraction of the swing, 0 to 1.
        low: f64,
        /// Upper fraction of the swing, 0 to 1.
        high: f64,
    },
    /// How long, from the start of the window, until the signal stays
    /// within `band` of its final value (or of `target`) to the end.
    Settling {
        /// The signal.
        signal: Signal,
        /// Allowed error either side, in the signal's unit.
        band: f64,
        /// The value it settles to; `None` takes the last sample.
        target: Option<f64>,
    },
    /// The first x after the peak where the signal, in dB, has fallen
    /// `drop_db` below that peak: the −3 dB point of a low-pass or the
    /// upper one of a band-pass, with `drop_db` 3.
    Bandwidth {
        /// The signal; read in dB whatever its view.
        signal: Signal,
        /// How far below the peak, in dB.
        drop_db: f64,
    },
}

impl Measure {
    /// A statistic of a signal.
    pub fn stat(signal: Signal, stat: Stat) -> Self { … }

    /// The signal's value at `at`.
    pub fn find(signal: Signal, at: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// 10–90 % rise time.
    pub fn rise_time(signal: Signal) -> Self { … }

    /// 90–10 % fall time.
    pub fn fall_time(signal: Signal) -> Self { … }

    /// Settling time to within `band` of the final value.
    pub fn settling(signal: Signal, band: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// The −3 dB point.
    pub fn bandwidth(signal: Signal) -> Self { … }
}

/// A named measurement, optionally limited to a window of x.
pub struct Measurement {
    /// Name, reported back with the value.
    pub name: String,
    /// What is measured.
    pub measure: Measure,
    /// Start of the window on the x axis; `None` is the start of the result.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub from: Option<f64>,
    /// End of the window; `None` is the end of the result.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub to: Option<f64>,
}

impl Measurement {
    /// A measurement over the whole result.
    pub fn new(name: impl Into<String>, measure: Measure) -> Self { … }

    /// Limit it to `from ≤ x ≤ to`.
    pub fn window(mut self, from: f64, to: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// Take the measurement on a result.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`SimError::Measurement`] when it can't be taken: an unknown node or
    /// component, a window outside the result, a level never crossed.
    pub fn on(&self, result: &impl Measurable) -> Result<f64, SimError> { … }
}

/// A measurement with limits: `V(vout)` 4.9–5.1 V, ripple under 50 mV.
pub struct Spec {
    /// What is measured; its name names the spec.
    pub measurement: Measurement,
    /// Lowest value that passes, inclusive. `None` for no lower limit.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub min: Option<f64>,
    /// Highest value that passes, inclusive. `None` for no upper limit.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub max: Option<f64>,
}

impl Spec {
    /// A spec with no limits yet. With none it passes whenever the
    /// measurement can be taken, which records a value in the report.
    pub fn new(measurement: Measurement) -> Self { … }

    /// Pass when `min ≤ value ≤ max`.
    pub fn between(mut self, min: f64, max: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// Pass when `value ≥ min`.
    pub fn at_least(mut self, min: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// Pass when `value ≤ max`.
    pub fn at_most(mut self, max: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// Measure on a result and judge it.
    pub fn check(&self, result: &impl Measurable) -> SpecCheck { … }
}

/// How a spec did.
pub enum SpecStatus {
    /// Within its limits.
    Pass,
    /// Outside them.
    Fail,
    /// The measurement couldn't be taken; [`SpecCheck::reason`] says why.
    /// Never counted as a pass.
    Unmeasured,
}

/// One spec checked against one result.
pub struct SpecCheck {
    /// The measurement's name.
    pub name: String,
    /// The measured value, in the signal's unit; `None` when unmeasured.
    pub value: Option<f64>,
    /// Lower limit.
    pub min: Option<f64>,
    /// Upper limit.
    pub max: Option<f64>,
    /// Distance to the nearer limit, in the signal's unit: positive inside
    /// the limits, negative outside. `None` with no limits or no value.
    pub margin: Option<f64>,
    /// Pass, fail or unmeasured.
    pub status: SpecStatus,
    /// Why the measurement couldn't be taken.
    pub reason: Option<String>,
}

/// Every spec's verdict, with the ratings checks alongside when attached.
pub struct SpecReport {
    /// One entry per spec, in the order given.
    pub checks: Vec<SpecCheck>,
    /// The ratings checks, when attached with [`with_ratings`](Self::with_ratings).
    pub ratings: Option<RatingsReport>,
}

impl SpecReport {
    /// Attach a ratings report, so [`passed`](Self::passed) also needs every
    /// part within its ratings.
    pub fn with_ratings(mut self, ratings: RatingsReport) -> Self { … }

    /// Join another report, such as the specs checked on a second analysis.
    /// Its ratings checks are appended to this one's.
    pub fn merge(mut self, other: SpecReport) -> Self { … }

    /// `true` only when every spec passed and, with ratings attached, every
    /// part is within them ([`RatingsReport::is_safe`]).
    pub fn passed(&self) -> bool { … }

    /// Specs outside their limits.
    pub fn failed(&self) -> Vec<&SpecCheck> { … }

    /// Specs whose measurement couldn't be taken.
    pub fn unmeasured(&self) -> Vec<&SpecCheck> { … }

    /// The check for one spec, by name.
    pub fn get(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&SpecCheck> { … }
}

/// Check every spec against a result.
///
/// A measurement that can't be taken is [`SpecStatus::Unmeasured`] with the
/// reason, not an error, so one bad spec doesn't hide the others' verdicts.
pub fn check_specs(result: &impl Measurable, specs: &[Spec]) -> SpecReport { … }
```

## `sindr/src/mna.rs`

Modified Nodal Analysis (MNA) matrix system.

Holds the `(n+m) × (n+m)` MNA matrix and right-hand-side vector that every
analysis path eventually solves, where `n` is the number of non-ground
nodes and `m` is the number of branch-current unknowns (independent
voltage sources, controlled sources that introduce a branch, etc.).

Components write themselves into this system via [`stamp`](crate::stamp);
the linear DC, Newton–Raphson, and transient pipelines all build an
[`MnaSystem`], stamp into it, and call [`MnaSystem::solve`].

The matrix is stored densely for small systems and as a sparse list of
entries above [`DENSE_MAX`] unknowns, where it is factorised with a sparse
LU. A circuit's sparsity pattern is the same from one Newton iteration or
timestep to the next, so the sparse LU's symbolic analysis is reused while
the pattern doesn't change.

```rust
/// Largest system (unknowns) stored and solved densely. Above it the matrix
/// is sparse. From `benches/mna_solve.rs`: dense and sparse cost about the
/// same at 100 unknowns (70 µs vs 35–80 µs), dense is 5–7× faster at 10, and
/// sparse is 50–250× faster at 1 000.
pub const DENSE_MAX: usize = 100;

/// A scalar the MNA matrix can hold: `f64` for DC and transient,
/// [`Complex64`] for AC.
pub trait MnaScalar:
    nalgebra::ComplexField<RealField = f64> + faer::traits::ComplexField + Copy
{
    /// Whether the value is finite (both parts, for a complex number).
    fn is_finite_value(&self) -> bool;
}

/// The `size × size` MNA matrix: indexed as `a[(row, col)]` and written with
/// `+=` by the stamps, whatever its storage.
pub struct MnaMatrix<T: MnaScalar = f64> {
    size: usize,
    storage: Storage<T>,
    /// Returned when reading an entry a sparse matrix doesn't hold.
    zero: T,
}

impl<T: MnaScalar> MnaMatrix<T> {
    /// A zero `size × size` matrix, dense if `size` ≤ [`DENSE_MAX`].
    pub fn zeros(size: usize) -> Self { … }

    /// A zero `size × size` matrix stored densely.
    pub fn dense(size: usize) -> Self { … }

    /// A zero `size × size` matrix stored sparsely.
    pub fn sparse(size: usize) -> Self { … }

    /// Number of rows (and columns).
    pub fn size(&self) -> usize { … }

    /// Whether the matrix is stored sparsely.
    pub fn is_sparse(&self) -> bool { … }

    /// The matrix as a dense nalgebra matrix.
    pub fn to_dense(&self) -> DMatrix<T> { … }

    /// The transpose of the matrix, in the same storage.
    pub fn transpose(&self) -> Self { … }

    /// Solve `self · x = b`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`SimError::SingularMatrix`] if the matrix is singular, or
    /// [`SimError::InvalidSolution`] if the solution contains NaN or Inf.
    pub fn solve(&self, b: &DVector<T>) -> Result<DVector<T>, SimError> { … }
}

/// Modified Nodal Analysis system.
///
/// Holds the (n+m)x(n+m) conductance/constraint matrix `a` and the (n+m)
/// right-hand-side vector `b`, where n = number of non-ground nodes and
/// m = number of independent voltage sources.
pub struct MnaSystem {
    /// (n+m)x(n+m) conductance/constraint matrix (siemens S in the node block).
    pub a: MnaMatrix<f64>,
    /// (n+m) right-hand-side vector (amperes A in the node block, volts V in the source block).
    pub b: DVector<f64>,
    /// Number of non-ground nodes (n).
    pub num_nodes: usize,
    /// Number of independent voltage sources contributing branch-current unknowns (m).
    pub num_vsources: usize,
}

impl MnaSystem {
    /// Create a zero-filled MNA system of the given dimensions, sparse above
    /// [`DENSE_MAX`] unknowns.
    pub fn new(num_nodes: usize, num_vsources: usize) -> Self { … }

    /// Total dimension of the system (n + m).
    pub fn size(&self) -> usize { … }

    /// Solve Ax = b: LU with partial pivoting, dense or sparse.
    ///
    /// Returns the solution vector on success.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`SimError::SingularMatrix`] if the matrix is singular, or
    /// [`SimError::InvalidSolution`] if the solution contains NaN or Inf.
    pub fn solve(&self) -> Result<DVector<f64>, SimError> { … }
}
```

## `sindr/src/newton_raphson.rs`

Newton-Raphson nonlinear solver.

Orchestrates iterative solving for circuits containing nonlinear
elements (diodes, BJTs, MOSFETs, JFETs, IGBTs, ...). Each iteration builds a fresh MNA system
with companion models evaluated at the current operating point,
solves it, applies voltage limiting, and checks convergence.

```rust
/// Maximum Newton-Raphson iterations before declaring non-convergence.
pub const MAX_NR_ITERATIONS: usize = 100;

/// Absolute voltage tolerance (V).
pub const V_ABSTOL: f64 = 1e-6;

/// Relative tolerance (dimensionless).
pub const RELTOL: f64 = 1e-3;

/// Solve a circuit containing nonlinear elements via Newton-Raphson iteration.
///
/// # Algorithm
///
/// 1. Start from the linear part of the circuit solved with the nonlinear
///    devices left out, then move each BJT base to a typical Vbe and cap each
///    forward-biased diode junction at its critical voltage, as SPICE does.
/// 2. Each iteration: stamp all components (with companion models at v_prev),
///    add Gmin shunts, solve, apply voltage limiting, check convergence.
///    When limiting one junction pushes a neighbour sharing its node past
///    its own limit (diodes in series), take a damped step that keeps every
///    junction within its limit instead.
/// 3. Converged when every node voltage has settled within
///    `V_ABSTOL + RELTOL·|V|` and every diode, LED and BJT junction voltage
///    within `V_ABSTOL + RELTOL·n·V_T`; error after [`MAX_NR_ITERATIONS`].
///
/// When plain Newton–Raphson fails, retries with gmin stepping and then
/// source stepping; [`SimulationResult::convergence_aid`] says which one
/// succeeded.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// [`SimError::ConvergenceFailed`] if plain Newton–Raphson, gmin stepping
/// and source stepping all fail, plus any stamping or solve error.
pub fn solve_nonlinear(
    circuit: &Circuit,
    node_map: &NodeMap,
    num_nodes: usize,
    num_vsources: usize,
) -> Result<SimulationResult, SimError> { … }

/// Like [`solve_nonlinear`] but seeds the Newton initial guess with the
/// supplied per-node voltages (V), keyed by node name. Equivalent to SPICE's
/// `.NODESET` directive — useful when a circuit has multiple operating
/// points or when default heuristics fail to converge. Unknown node names
/// are silently ignored; nodes not in the map fall back to the default
/// initialisation.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// As [`solve_nonlinear`].
pub fn solve_nonlinear_with_initial_voltages(
    circuit: &Circuit,
    node_map: &NodeMap,
    num_nodes: usize,
    num_vsources: usize,
    initial_voltages: &std::collections::HashMap<String, f64>,
) -> Result<SimulationResult, SimError> { … }
```

## `sindr/src/node_map.rs`

Node-name ↔ matrix-index mapping.

MNA matrices are indexed by integer; circuits are described in terms of
arbitrary node-name strings. [`NodeMap`] is the bidirectional translation
table between the two. The ground node is excluded from the matrix and
maps to `None` — every other unique node string gets a sequential index.

```rust
/// Maps circuit node names to MNA matrix indices.
///
/// The ground node is excluded from the matrix (maps to `None`).
/// All other nodes receive sequential zero-based indices.
pub struct NodeMap {
    map: HashMap<String, usize>,
    reverse: Vec<String>,
    ground: String,
}

impl NodeMap {
    /// Build a `NodeMap` by extracting all unique nodes from a [`Circuit`].
    ///
    /// Nodes are sorted alphabetically (via `BTreeSet`) before index
    /// assignment to ensure deterministic, reproducible ordering.
    pub fn from_circuit(circuit: &Circuit) -> Self { … }

    /// Build a `NodeMap` from a list of node names and a ground node name.
    ///
    /// The ground node is filtered out; remaining nodes are assigned
    /// sequential indices starting from 0.
    pub fn from_nodes(nodes: &[String], ground: &str) -> Self { … }

    /// Look up the matrix index for a node.
    ///
    /// Returns `None` for the ground node, `Some(index)` for all others.
    pub fn index(&self, node: &str) -> Option<usize> { … }

    /// Number of non-ground nodes (i.e. the number of node-voltage unknowns).
    pub fn num_nodes(&self) -> usize { … }

    /// Reverse lookup: get the node name for a given matrix index.
    pub fn node_name(&self, index: usize) -> Option<&str> { … }
}
```

## `sindr/src/noise.rs`

Noise analysis, SPICE's `.noise`: thermal, shot and flicker noise at an
output voltage, and referred back to an input source.

Every noise source is a current between two nodes with a power spectral
density (A²/Hz), set by the DC operating point:

| Component | Source | Between | PSD |
|---|---|---|---|
| resistor, potentiometer (each half), thermistor, photoresistor | thermal | its terminals | `4kT/R` |
| diode, LED, Schottky, Zener, photodiode | shot | anode–cathode | `2q·\|I\|` |
| diode with a `model` | flicker | anode–cathode | `KF·\|I\|^AF / f` |
| BJT | shot | collector–emitter, base–emitter | `2q·\|Ic\|`, `2q·\|Ib\|` |
| BJT with a `model` | flicker | base–emitter | `KF·\|Ib\|^AF / f` |
| MOSFET | channel thermal | drain–source | `(8/3)·kT·gm` |
| MOSFET | flicker | drain–source | `KF·\|Id\|^AF / f` |
| JFET | channel thermal | drain–source | `(8/3)·kT·gm` |

`T` is 300.15 K (27 °C), as in SPICE, except that a thermistor's thermal
noise uses its own temperature. Sources, controlled sources, op-amps,
regulators, switches, fuses, IGBTs and a diode's series resistance are
noiseless.

At each frequency one adjoint solve, `Aᵀ·y = e_out`, gives the transfer
from a unit current at every node to the output. Each source then adds
`|y_p − y_q|²·PSD` to the output's PSD. One forward solve from the input
source gives the gain that refers the output noise back to the input.
Integrated noise assumes each PSD follows a power law between points, as
ngspice does.

```rust
/// Noise analysis configuration: SPICE's
/// `.noise V(output[,reference]) input_source {dec|lin} points f_start f_stop`.
pub struct NoiseConfig {
    /// The output node.
    pub output: String,
    /// The node the output is measured against; ground when `None`.
    pub reference: Option<String>,
    /// The independent voltage or current source noise is referred back to.
    pub input_source: String,
    /// Start frequency (Hz), above 0: flicker noise is infinite at DC.
    pub f_start: f64,
    /// Stop frequency (Hz).
    pub f_stop: f64,
    /// Number of frequency points, both ends included.
    pub num_points: usize,
    /// Frequency spacing; logarithmic is `num_points` in total.
    pub spacing: FrequencySpacing,
}

/// The physical mechanism behind a noise source.
pub enum NoiseKind {
    /// Johnson–Nyquist noise of a resistance, or a FET channel's.
    Thermal,
    /// Shot noise of a current crossing a junction.
    Shot,
    /// Flicker (1/f) noise.
    Flicker,
}

/// One noise source in the circuit.
pub struct NoiseSource {
    /// Component id (flattened).
    pub component: String,
    /// Which mechanism.
    pub kind: NoiseKind,
    /// Which current it sits on, for parts with more than one: `"ic"`,
    /// `"ib"`, `"top"`/`"bottom"` for a potentiometer; empty otherwise.
    pub branch: &'static str,
}

/// Noise at one frequency.
pub struct NoisePoint {
    /// Frequency (Hz).
    pub frequency: f64,
    /// Output noise power spectral density (V²/Hz).
    pub output_psd: f64,
    /// Noise referred to the input source (V²/Hz for a voltage source,
    /// A²/Hz for a current source): `output_psd / |gain|²`. Infinite where
    /// the gain is zero.
    pub input_psd: f64,
    /// The gain from the input source to the output, `|V(out)/input|`.
    pub gain: f64,
    /// Each source's share of `output_psd` (V²/Hz), in the order of
    /// [`NoiseResult::sources`].
    pub contributions: Vec<f64>,
}

impl NoisePoint {
    /// Output noise density (V/√Hz), what ngspice calls `onoise_spectrum`.
    pub fn output_density(&self) -> f64 { … }

    /// Input-referred noise density (V/√Hz or A/√Hz): `inoise_spectrum`.
    pub fn input_density(&self) -> f64 { … }
}

/// Result of a noise analysis.
pub struct NoiseResult {
    /// Every noise source, in the order of [`NoisePoint::contributions`].
    pub sources: Vec<NoiseSource>,
    /// One point per frequency.
    pub points: Vec<NoisePoint>,
    /// Output noise integrated over the band (V rms): `onoise_total`.
    pub total_output_noise: f64,
    /// Input-referred noise integrated over the band (V or A rms):
    /// `inoise_total`.
    pub total_input_noise: f64,
    /// Each source's output noise integrated over the band (V rms), in the
    /// order of [`sources`](Self::sources).
    pub source_totals: Vec<f64>,
    /// Configuration used to produce this result.
    pub config: NoiseConfig,
}

/// Runs a noise analysis, as SPICE's `.noise`. See the [module docs](self)
/// for the sources and the method.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// - [`SimError::InvalidComponent`] if the input isn't an independent
///   voltage or current source, an output node isn't in the circuit, or
///   the frequencies are invalid (`f_start` must be above 0)
/// - Any [`SimError`] from the DC operating point
/// - [`SimError::SingularMatrix`] if the linearised system is singular
///
/// # Example
///
/// ```
/// use sindr::{Circuit, CircuitElement};
/// use sindr::ac_analysis::FrequencySpacing;
/// use sindr::noise::{solve_noise, NoiseConfig};
///
/// // A 1 kΩ / 1 µF low-pass: the output noise integrates to √(kT/C).
/// let circuit = Circuit::new("0", vec![
///     CircuitElement::VoltageSource { id: "V1".into(), nodes: ["in".into(), "0".into()], voltage: 0.0, waveform: None },
///     CircuitElement::Resistor { id: "R1".into(), nodes: ["in".into(), "out".into()], resistance: 1e3 },
///     CircuitElement::Capacitor { id: "C1".into(), nodes: ["out".into(), "0".into()], capacitance: 1e-6 },
/// ]);
/// let noise = solve_noise(&circuit, &NoiseConfig {
///     output: "out".into(),
///     reference: None,
///     input_source: "V1".into(),
///     f_start: 0.01,
///     f_stop: 1e7,
///     num_points: 91,
///     spacing: FrequencySpacing::Logarithmic,
/// })?;
/// let kt_over_c = (1.380649e-23 * 300.15 / 1e-6_f64).sqrt();
/// assert!((noise.total_output_noise / kt_over_c - 1.0).abs() < 0.01);
/// # Ok::<(), sindr::SimError>(())
/// ```
pub fn solve_noise(circuit: &Circuit, config: &NoiseConfig) -> Result<NoiseResult, SimError> { … }

/// [`solve_noise`], seeding the bias point's Newton–Raphson solve as
/// `.nodeset` does.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// As [`solve_noise`].
pub fn solve_noise_with_initial_voltages(
    circuit: &Circuit,
    config: &NoiseConfig,
    initial_voltages: &HashMap<String, f64>,
) -> Result<NoiseResult, SimError> { … }
```

## `sindr/src/ratings.rs`

Absolute-maximum ratings checks: did any part go past its datasheet
limits?

[`check_ratings`] compares a [`SimulationResult`] against the
[`Ratings`] on each component's [`Part`](crate::Part) (looked up by
component id in [`Circuit::parts`]). It looks at the DC operating point,
or at every step of a transient, since peaks (inrush, inductive
kickback, start-up) are what kill parts. For each part and rating it
reports the worst value, when it happened, the limit and the margin left.

Each component kind has ratings it needs, which are checked whether set
or not. A needed rating that isn't set comes back
[`RatingStatus::Unverified`], never as a pass:

| Component | Needs |
|---|---|
| resistor, potentiometer, thermistor, photoresistor | `power` |
| capacitor | `voltage` |
| inductor | `current` |
| diode, Schottky, LED, photodiode | `reverse_voltage`, `forward_current`, `power` |
| Zener | `power` |
| varactor | `reverse_voltage` |
| BJT | `vce`, `vcb`, `veb`, `ic`, `power` |
| MOSFET, JFET | `vds`, `vgs`, `id`, `power` |
| IGBT | `vce`, `vgs` (gate–emitter), `ic`, `power` |
| voltage regulator | `voltage` (input, from its ground pin), `current` (output), `power` |

A part with [`Thermal`](crate::Thermal) data also needs `tj_max`, checked
against the junction temperature self-heating reports. Without thermal
data there is no junction temperature, so a `tj_max` is unverified.

Any other rating a part sets is checked as well. `power`, `voltage` and
`current` work on every component, measured on the port its
[`ComponentResult`] reports (Vce and Ic for a BJT). A rating the
component has no way to measure, such as `vds` on a resistor, is
unverified. Transistor power is `|V·I|` on that port, so a BJT's base
dissipation is left out.

```
use sindr::{check_ratings, solve_circuit, Circuit, CircuitElement, Part, Ratings};

let mut circuit = Circuit::new(
    "0",
    vec![
        CircuitElement::VoltageSource { id: "V1".into(), nodes: ["in".into(), "0".into()], voltage: 12.0, waveform: None },
        CircuitElement::Resistor { id: "R1".into(), nodes: ["in".into(), "0".into()], resistance: 100.0 },
    ],
);
// A 1/8 W resistor across 12 V dissipates 1.44 W.
circuit.parts.insert(
    "R1".into(),
    Part { ratings: Ratings { power: Some(0.125), ..Ratings::default() }, ..Part::default() },
);

let result = solve_circuit(&circuit).unwrap();
let report = check_ratings(&circuit, &result).unwrap();
let r1 = &report.exceeded()[0];
assert_eq!(r1.part, "R1");
assert!((r1.worst.unwrap() - 1.44).abs() < 1e-9);
assert!(!report.is_safe());
```

```rust
/// One absolute-maximum rating. Each is a magnitude; see [`Ratings`] for
/// what it measures.
pub enum RatingKind {
    /// Power dissipation (W).
    Power,
    /// Voltage across the part (V).
    Voltage,
    /// Current through the part (A).
    Current,
    /// Diode reverse voltage (V).
    ReverseVoltage,
    /// Diode forward current (A).
    ForwardCurrent,
    /// Collector–emitter voltage (V).
    Vce,
    /// Collector–base voltage (V).
    Vcb,
    /// Emitter–base voltage (V).
    Veb,
    /// Collector current (A).
    Ic,
    /// Drain–source voltage (V).
    Vds,
    /// Gate–source (or IGBT gate–emitter) voltage (V).
    Vgs,
    /// Drain current (A).
    Id,
    /// Junction temperature (K), from self-heating.
    Tj,
}

impl RatingKind {
    /// The limit `ratings` sets for this kind, if any.
    pub fn limit(self, ratings: &Ratings) -> Option<f64> { … }

    /// SI unit symbol: `"W"`, `"V"`, `"A"` or `"K"`.
    pub fn unit(self) -> &'static str { … }
}

/// How a part did against one rating.
pub enum RatingStatus {
    /// The worst value stayed at or under the limit.
    Within,
    /// The worst value went over the limit.
    Exceeded,
    /// Can't tell: the rating isn't set, or sindr can't measure it on this
    /// component.
    Unverified,
}

/// One part checked against one rating.
pub struct RatingCheck {
    /// Component id, flattened (`X1.Q1`).
    pub part: String,
    /// Which rating.
    pub rating: RatingKind,
    /// The limit, in the rating's unit. `None` when the part doesn't set it.
    pub limit: Option<f64>,
    /// The worst (largest) value the part saw, in the rating's unit. `None`
    /// when sindr can't measure it on this component.
    pub worst: Option<f64>,
    /// When the worst value happened (s). `None` for a DC operating point.
    pub time: Option<f64>,
    /// Margin left, as a percentage of the limit: `100·(limit − worst)/limit`.
    /// Negative when exceeded; `None` when unverified.
    pub margin_percent: Option<f64>,
    /// Within, exceeded or unverified.
    pub status: RatingStatus,
}

/// Every rating checked on every part, in circuit order.
pub struct RatingsReport {
    /// One entry per part and rating.
    pub checks: Vec<RatingCheck>,
}

impl RatingsReport {
    /// Checks whose worst value went over the limit.
    pub fn exceeded(&self) -> Vec<&RatingCheck> { … }

    /// Checks that couldn't be verified.
    pub fn unverified(&self) -> Vec<&RatingCheck> { … }

    /// `true` only when every check is within its limit: nothing exceeded
    /// and nothing unverified.
    pub fn is_safe(&self) -> bool { … }

    /// The checks for one part.
    pub fn for_part<'a>(&'a self, part: &'a str) -> impl Iterator<Item = &'a RatingCheck> + 'a { … }
}

/// Check every component of `circuit` against the [`Ratings`] on its
/// [`Part`](crate::Part), using `result` from any solve of that circuit.
///
/// With a transient in `result`, every timestep is checked (the first is
/// the starting operating point); otherwise the DC operating point is. See
/// the [module docs](self) for which ratings each component needs.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// [`SimError::Design`] when the circuit's hierarchy can't be flattened.
pub fn check_ratings(
    circuit: &Circuit,
    result: &SimulationResult,
) -> Result<RatingsReport, SimError> { … }
```

## `sindr/src/results.rs`

Solver output types.

[`SimulationResult`] is what every analysis path returns: node voltages,
branch currents, per-component V/I/P, and (when relevant) per-device
operating-point detail and a transient time-series. The optional
per-device fields are populated only when the matching component types
appear in the circuit.

```rust
/// Per-component voltage, current, and power.
///
/// Reported for every component. For a two-terminal one, current flows
/// from `nodes[0]` to `nodes[1]` and positive `power` means it is
/// dissipating energy. Components with more terminals report one port:
/// BJTs and IGBTs give Vce and Ic, MOSFETs and JFETs give Vds and Id, with
/// `power` as the magnitude `|V·I|` (their full results are in
/// [`BjtResult`] and [`MosfetResult`]); a relay gives its coil, a
/// transformer its primary, and a voltage regulator its pass element
/// (`Vin − Vout`, the output current, and its dissipation).
pub struct ComponentResult {
    /// Component id (matches the id on the source [`CircuitElement`]).
    pub id: String,
    /// Voltage from `nodes[0]` to `nodes[1]` (V).
    pub voltage_across: f64,
    /// Current from `nodes[0]` to `nodes[1]` (A).
    pub current_through: f64,
    /// Instantaneous power dissipation (W). Positive = dissipating.
    pub power: f64,
}

/// Per-BJT operating-point results: terminal voltages, terminal currents,
/// power, and which region of operation the device is in.
pub struct BjtResult {
    /// Component id.
    pub id: String,
    /// Base–emitter voltage (V).
    pub vbe: f64,
    /// Collector–emitter voltage (V).
    pub vce: f64,
    /// Base current (A), into the base: positive for a conducting NPN,
    /// negative for a PNP.
    pub ib: f64,
    /// Collector current (A), into the collector: positive for a
    /// conducting NPN, negative for a PNP.
    pub ic: f64,
    /// Emitter current (A), into the emitter: `−(ic + ib)` by KCL, so
    /// negative for a conducting NPN and positive for a PNP.
    pub ie: f64,
    /// Collector dissipation `|Ic·Vce|` (W). The base's `Ib·Vbe` is left
    /// out.
    pub power: f64,
    /// Operating region: `"active"`, `"saturation"`, or `"cutoff"`.
    pub region: String,
}

/// Per-MOSFET operating-point results.
pub struct MosfetResult {
    /// Component id.
    pub id: String,
    /// Gate–source voltage (V).
    pub vgs: f64,
    /// Drain–source voltage (V).
    pub vds: f64,
    /// Drain current (A), into the drain: positive for a conducting NMOS,
    /// negative for a PMOS.
    pub id_current: f64,
    /// Total dissipation (W).
    pub power: f64,
    /// Operating region: `"cutoff"`, `"triode"`, or `"saturation"`.
    pub region: String,
}

/// Per-op-amp / comparator results: input/output voltages.
pub struct OpAmpResult {
    /// Component id.
    pub id: String,
    /// Voltage at the non-inverting input (V).
    pub v_in_plus: f64,
    /// Voltage at the inverting input (V).
    pub v_in_minus: f64,
    /// `v_in_plus - v_in_minus` (V).
    pub v_differential: f64,
    /// Output voltage (V), clipped to the rail range.
    pub v_out: f64,
}

/// Per-relay results: coil voltage and contact state.
pub struct RelayResult {
    /// Component id.
    pub id: String,
    /// Coil voltage, `coil+ − coil−` (`nodes[0] − nodes[1]`) (V).
    pub coil_voltage: f64,
    /// `true` when coil voltage exceeds the pickup threshold.
    pub contact_closed: bool,
}

/// Per-microcontroller results: per-pin GPIO output currents.
///
/// Never filled: sindr has no microcontroller element, so
/// [`SimulationResult::mcu_results`] is always empty.
pub struct McuResult {
    /// Component id.
    pub id: String,
    /// Current sourced/sunk by each GPIO pin (A), in pin index order.
    pub pin_currents: Vec<f64>,
    /// GPIO logic-high voltage used for this MCU (V).
    pub gpio_voltage: f64,
}

/// One timestep of a transient simulation: time, node voltages, per-component
/// state at that instant.
pub struct TimestepSnapshot {
    /// Simulation time at this snapshot (s).
    pub time: f64,
    /// Node voltages at this instant (V).
    pub node_voltages: HashMap<String, f64>,
    /// Per-component voltage/current/power at this instant. A source with a
    /// waveform reports its value at this time, not its DC term.
    pub component_results: Vec<ComponentResult>,
    /// Junction temperature (K) of each part with
    /// [`Thermal`](crate::Thermal) data at this instant, by component id.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(skip_serializing_if = "HashMap::is_empty", default)
    )]
    pub junction_temperatures: HashMap<String, f64>,
    /// State of charge (0 to 1) of each battery at this instant, by
    /// component id. Below 0 the cell is over-discharged; its voltage holds
    /// the curve's 0 % value.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(skip_serializing_if = "HashMap::is_empty", default)
    )]
    pub state_of_charge: HashMap<String, f64>,
}

/// Time-series data from a transient simulation.
///
/// Present on [`SimulationResult::transient`] when the circuit contains
/// reactive elements (capacitors, inductors) or time-varying sources.
pub struct TransientData {
    /// Snapshots at each accepted integration step, in time order. They
    /// include every multiple of `time_step`, every waveform breakpoint and
    /// the end time, plus any shorter steps accuracy needed in between.
    pub timesteps: Vec<TimestepSnapshot>,
    /// Requested time step (s): the longest step taken, and the output grid.
    pub time_step: f64,
    /// Total simulated duration (s).
    pub duration: f64,
    /// How the stepper got there.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub stats: TransientStats,
}

/// Step counts from one transient run.
pub struct TransientStats {
    /// Steps accepted (one snapshot each).
    pub accepted_steps: usize,
    /// Steps rejected because their local truncation error was too large.
    pub lte_rejections: usize,
    /// Steps retried at half the size because Newton–Raphson didn't converge.
    pub newton_rejections: usize,
}

/// Complete simulation output.
///
/// At minimum, contains node voltages, branch currents (for voltage sources
/// and other branch-current-bearing elements), and per-component results.
/// The optional fields are populated only when the corresponding
/// component types appear in the circuit:
///
/// - `bjt_results` — for [`Bjt`](crate::CircuitElement::Bjt) components
/// - `mosfet_results` — for [`Mosfet`](crate::CircuitElement::Mosfet)
/// - `op_amp_results` — for op-amps and comparators
/// - `relay_results` — for relays
/// - `mcu_results` — for microcontrollers
/// - `transient` — for circuits with capacitors, inductors, or waveform
///   sources (DC analysis returns `None`)
pub struct SimulationResult {
    /// Voltage at every node (V), keyed by node name. Includes the ground
    /// node (always 0.0).
    ///
    /// Indexing with `[]` panics on a missing key, the same as any
    /// [`HashMap`]. If the node name might be absent (e.g. typos, or a
    /// node only referenced via a control terminal), use
    /// `node_voltages.get("n2")` to get an `Option<&f64>` instead.
    pub node_voltages: HashMap<String, f64>,
    /// Branch currents (A) for components that introduce a current unknown
    /// — voltage sources, op-amps, transformers, etc. Keyed by component id.
    ///
    /// The MNA convention: the current entering the element at `nodes[0]`
    /// and leaving at `nodes[1]`, through the element. A source delivering
    /// power reads **negative**: a 5 V supply feeding 5 mA into a load is
    /// `-0.005`. For a VCVS, CCVS, op-amp or comparator it is the current
    /// into the output node (`nodes[0]`, or the op-amp's `out`), so an
    /// output sourcing current is negative too. For a voltage regulator it
    /// is the current into its output pin (negative when it sources); its
    /// [`ComponentResult`] has the output current as a positive number.
    pub branch_currents: HashMap<String, f64>,
    /// Per-component voltage, current, and power for every two-terminal
    /// component.
    pub component_results: Vec<ComponentResult>,
    /// Detailed per-BJT results. Empty when the circuit has no BJTs.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty", default)
    )]
    pub bjt_results: Vec<BjtResult>,
    /// Detailed per-MOSFET results. Empty when the circuit has no MOSFETs.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty", default)
    )]
    pub mosfet_results: Vec<MosfetResult>,
    /// Detailed per-op-amp / comparator results.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty", default)
    )]
    pub op_amp_results: Vec<OpAmpResult>,
    /// Detailed per-relay results.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty", default)
    )]
    pub relay_results: Vec<RelayResult>,
    /// Detailed per-microcontroller results.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty", default)
    )]
    pub mcu_results: Vec<McuResult>,
    /// Transient time-series, present only when the circuit has reactive
    /// elements or waveform sources.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub transient: Option<TransientData>,
    /// The fallback the nonlinear DC solve needed, if plain Newton–Raphson
    /// didn't converge on its own. `None` for linear circuits, transients and
    /// plain Newton.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none", default)
    )]
    pub convergence_aid: Option<ConvergenceAid>,
    /// Self-heated junction temperature (K) of each part with
    /// [`Thermal`](crate::Thermal) data, by component id: the DC balance, or
    /// the end of a transient. Empty when no part has thermal data.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(skip_serializing_if = "HashMap::is_empty", default)
    )]
    pub junction_temperatures: HashMap<String, f64>,
    /// State of charge (0 to 1) of each battery, by component id: the
    /// starting value at DC, the last step's after a transient.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(skip_serializing_if = "HashMap::is_empty", default)
    )]
    pub state_of_charge: HashMap<String, f64>,
}

/// A convergence fallback for nonlinear DC, tried in this order when plain
/// Newton–Raphson fails.
pub enum ConvergenceAid {
    /// Extra conductance to ground on every node, stepped from 1e-2 S down
    /// to zero.
    GminStepping,
    /// Every independent source ramped from near zero up to its full value.
    SourceStepping,
}

/// Extract simulation results from the MNA solution vector.
///
/// Builds node voltages, branch currents (for voltage sources), and
/// per-component V/I/P using passive sign convention.
pub fn extract_results(
    circuit: &Circuit,
    node_map: &NodeMap,
    solution: &DVector<f64>,
    num_nodes: usize,
) -> SimulationResult { … }
```

## `sindr/src/sensitivity.rs`

DC sensitivity analysis, as SPICE's `.sens`.

The derivative of one DC output with respect to each component parameter,
at the operating point. With the linearised system `A` and the output
`y = cᵀx`, one adjoint solve `Aᵀλ = c` gives every parameter's derivative
as `dy/dp = λᵀ(∂b/∂p − (∂A/∂p)·x)`, so the cost doesn't grow with the
number of parameters.

```rust
/// Sensitivity-analysis configuration.
pub struct SensConfig {
    /// The output whose sensitivities are wanted.
    pub output: TfOutput,
}

/// Which parameter of a component a [`SensEntry`] is for.
pub enum SensParameter {
    /// A resistor's resistance (Ω).
    Resistance,
    /// A voltage source's DC voltage (V).
    Voltage,
    /// A current source's DC current (A).
    Current,
    /// A VCVS's gain (V/V).
    VoltageGain,
    /// A VCCS's transconductance (S).
    Transconductance,
}

/// The sensitivity of the output to one component parameter.
pub struct SensEntry {
    /// Id of the component.
    pub component_id: String,
    /// Which of its parameters.
    pub parameter: SensParameter,
    /// The parameter's value, in its own unit.
    pub value: f64,
    /// d(output)/d(parameter): the output's unit (V or A) per the
    /// parameter's unit.
    pub sensitivity: f64,
    /// Change in the output, in its own unit, for a 1 % rise in the
    /// parameter: `sensitivity · value / 100`.
    pub per_percent: f64,
}

/// Result of a sensitivity analysis.
pub struct SensResult {
    /// One entry per supported parameter, in circuit order. Components with
    /// no entry: see [`solve_sensitivity`].
    pub entries: Vec<SensEntry>,
    /// Configuration used to produce this result.
    pub config: SensConfig,
}

impl SensResult {
    /// The entry for the component `id`.
    pub fn get(&self, id: &str) -> Option<&SensEntry> { … }
}

/// Runs a DC sensitivity analysis, as SPICE's `.sens`.
///
/// Reports resistors' resistance, voltage and current sources' DC value,
/// VCVS gain and VCCS transconductance. Other components stay in the
/// linearised circuit but get no entry: device-model parameters (IS, β, ...),
/// CCVS and CCCS gains, capacitors and inductors, which have no effect at DC
/// apart from the 1 TΩ leak a capacitor is given.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// - [`SimError::InvalidComponent`] if the output node is not in the circuit,
///   or a current output does not name an independent voltage source
/// - Any [`SimError`] from the DC operating-point solve
/// - [`SimError::SingularMatrix`] if the linearised system is singular
///
/// # Example
///
/// ```
/// use sindr::{solve_sensitivity, Circuit, CircuitElement, SensConfig, TfOutput};
///
/// // 4 V over 1 kΩ / 3 kΩ: V(out) = V1 · R2 / (R1 + R2) = 3 V.
/// let circuit = Circuit {
///     ground_node: "0".into(),
///     components: vec![
