/// The default is sindr's built-in silicon diode. With serde, a missing field
/// takes its default, so `{"rs": 0.5}` is a silicon diode with 0.5 Ω in series.
pub struct DiodeModel {
    /// Saturation current IS (A), positive. Default 1e-14.
    pub is: f64,
    /// Emission coefficient N, positive. Default 1.
    pub n: f64,
    /// Series resistance RS (Ω), zero or positive. Default 0.
    pub rs: f64,
    /// Zero-bias depletion capacitance CJO (F), zero or positive. Default 0.
    pub cjo: f64,
    /// Junction potential VJ (V), positive. Default 1.
    pub vj: f64,
    /// Grading coefficient M, in `[0, 0.9]`. Default 0.5.
    pub m: f64,
    /// Forward-bias depletion capacitance coefficient FC, in `[0, 0.95]`.
    /// Default 0.5.
    pub fc: f64,
    /// Transit time TT (s), zero or positive: the diffusion charge is
    /// `TT·I_d`, which sets reverse recovery. Default 0.
    pub tt: f64,
    /// Reverse breakdown voltage BV (V), positive. Default `None`: no
    /// breakdown, as in SPICE without `BV`.
    pub bv: Option<f64>,
    /// Current at `−BV`, IBV (A), positive. Default 1 mA.
    pub ibv: f64,
    /// Flicker-noise coefficient KF, zero or positive: noise analysis puts
    /// `KF·|Id|^AF / f` (A²/Hz) across the junction. Default 0.
    pub kf: f64,
    /// Flicker-noise exponent AF, positive. Default 1.
    pub af: f64,
}

impl DiodeModel {
    /// Whether the diode stores charge (CJO or TT set), which makes the
    /// circuit reactive.
    pub fn stores_charge(&self) -> bool { … }
}

/// Ebers–Moll parameters of a [`CircuitElement::Bjt`], as a SPICE
/// `.model NPN`/`PNP` card gives them. The forward gain is the element's own
/// `bf`. Values are at the nominal 27 °C; the element's `temperature` scales
/// `is` from there.
///
/// The default is sindr's built-in transistor. With serde, a missing field
/// takes its default.
pub struct BjtModel {
    /// Transport saturation current IS (A), positive. Default 1e-14.
    pub is: f64,
    /// Reverse current gain BR, positive. Default 1.
    pub br: f64,
    /// Forward emission coefficient NF, positive. Default 1.
    pub nf: f64,
    /// Reverse emission coefficient NR, positive. Default 1.
    pub nr: f64,
    /// Forward Early voltage VAF (V), zero or positive; 0 turns the Early
    /// effect off. Default 0. sindr applies it as `ic·(1 + vce/VAF)`, not
    /// through SPICE's Gummel–Poon base charge, so results differ slightly
    /// from SPICE's when it is set.
    pub vaf: f64,
    /// Flicker-noise coefficient KF, zero or positive: noise analysis puts
    /// `KF·|Ib|^AF / f` (A²/Hz) across base–emitter. Default 0.
    pub kf: f64,
    /// Flicker-noise exponent AF, positive. Default 1.
    pub af: f64,
}

/// MOSFET gate parasitic capacitances. All values in Farads.
/// Op-amp macromodel parameters, for [`CircuitElement::OpAmp`]'s `model`.
///
/// The gain stage is a first-order lag towards `gain · (v₊ − v₋ + offset)`,
/// clamped to the rails, with time constant `gain / (2π · gbw)`: open-loop
/// gain `gain / (1 + s·τ)`, so a non-inverting stage of gain G has its
/// −3 dB point near `gbw / G`. Its rate is limited to `slew_rate`. The
/// output is that stage's voltage behind `r_out`.
///
/// The pole and the slew limit act in transient and AC analyses. At DC the
/// stage sits at its clamped target. The op-amp's state doesn't count as
/// reactive, so [`solve_circuit`]-style automatic routing still picks DC
/// for a circuit whose only dynamics are op-amps; run a transient
/// explicitly to see them. Like capacitors, the stage starts from rest
/// (0 V) at t = 0.
///
/// [`solve_circuit`]: https://docs.rs/sindr/latest/sindr/fn.solve_circuit.html
pub struct OpAmpModel {
    /// Open-loop DC gain (V/V), positive. Default 1e5 (100 dB).
    pub gain: f64,
    /// Gain-bandwidth product (Hz), positive; `None` for no pole. Default
    /// 1 MHz.
    pub gbw: Option<f64>,
    /// Slew rate (V/s), positive; `None` for no limit. Needs `gbw`.
    /// Default 0.5 V/µs.
    pub slew_rate: Option<f64>,
    /// Output resistance (Ω), zero or positive. Default 0.
    pub r_out: f64,
    /// Input offset voltage (V), added to `v₊ − v₋`. Default 0.
    pub offset_voltage: f64,
    /// Input bias current (A) drawn by each input, to ground. Default 0.
    pub bias_current: f64,
}

pub struct MosfetParasiticCaps {
    /// Gate-Source capacitance (F). Typical: 100–500 pF for power MOSFETs.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub cgs: f64,
    /// Gate-Drain capacitance (Miller capacitance) (F). Typical: 10–100 pF.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub cgd: f64,
}

/// A single circuit component.
///
/// Each variant carries an `id` (unique per circuit, used to look up results)
/// and a `nodes` array naming its terminals. Node names are arbitrary
/// strings — components share a node by referencing the same string.
///
/// # Sign conventions
///
/// - **Two-terminal components** (resistor, source, capacitor, …):
///   `nodes[0]` is the positive / first terminal, `nodes[1]` is the
///   negative / second.
/// - **Polarised components** (voltage/current sources, diodes, BJTs, …):
///   exact terminal order is documented per variant.
/// - **Currents** are reported as flowing from `nodes[0]` to `nodes[1]` for
///   two-terminal components.
///
/// # Serde
///
/// With the default `serde` feature enabled, `CircuitElement` serialises
/// using a `type` discriminator: `{"type": "resistor", "id": "R1", ...}`.
pub enum CircuitElement {
    /// Resistor between two nodes.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "resistor"))]
    Resistor {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[a, b]`.
        nodes: [String; 2],
        /// Resistance (Ω).
        resistance: f64,
    },

    /// Independent voltage source. `nodes[0]` is the positive terminal,
    /// `nodes[1]` is the negative terminal.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "voltage_source"))]
    VoltageSource {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[positive, negative]`.
        nodes: [String; 2],
        /// DC voltage (V); also the offset added to any `waveform`.
        voltage: f64,
        /// Optional time-varying waveform added on top of `voltage`.
        #[cfg_attr(
            feature = "serde",
            serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
        )]
        waveform: Option<Waveform>,
    },

    /// Independent current source. Current flows from `nodes[0]` toward
    /// `nodes[1]`.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "current_source"))]
    CurrentSource {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[from, to]`; current flows from `nodes[0]` to `nodes[1]`.
        nodes: [String; 2],
        /// DC current (A); also the offset added to any `waveform`.
        current: f64,
        /// Optional time-varying waveform added on top of `current`.
        #[cfg_attr(
            feature = "serde",
            serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
        )]
        waveform: Option<Waveform>,
    },

    /// Switch between two nodes. Modeled as a resistor with very low (closed)
    /// or very high (open) resistance for DC analysis.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "switch"))]
    Switch {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[a, b]`.
        nodes: [String; 2],
        /// When true the switch conducts (closed); when false it is open.
        closed: bool,
    },

    /// Capacitor. Open-circuit in DC analysis; charges/discharges in
    /// transient. `voltage_across` is reported as `nodes[0] − nodes[1]`.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "capacitor"))]
    Capacitor {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[a, b]`.
        nodes: [String; 2],
        /// Capacitance (F).
        capacitance: f64,
    },

    /// A battery: open-circuit voltage by state of charge behind a series
    /// resistance and an optional RC pair ([`BatteryParams`]). At DC it is
    /// its open-circuit voltage at `state_of_charge` behind `R0 + R1`. In
    /// transient the RC pair charges and the state of charge falls with the
    /// charge drawn, reported per step in `state_of_charge`. In AC it is
    /// the impedance `R0 + R1‖C1`. `current_through` flows
    /// `nodes[0] → nodes[1]` inside the cell, so it is negative while the
    /// battery discharges, as for a voltage source.
    ///
    /// [`BatteryParams`]: sindr_devices::battery::BatteryParams
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "battery"))]
    Battery {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[positive, negative]`.
        nodes: [String; 2],
        /// The cell's equivalent circuit.
        params: sindr_devices::battery::BatteryParams,
        /// State of charge at the start, 0 (empty) to 1 (full).
        state_of_charge: f64,
    },

    /// Inductor. Stamped as **open-circuit in pure DC analysis** (sindr
    /// solves DC as a single algebraic step, not as t→∞ of a transient);
    /// integrates `dI/dt` properly during transient. The DC bias point that
    /// AC, `.tf` and `.sens` linearise around shorts it instead. `voltage_across` is
    /// reported as `nodes[0] − nodes[1]`, `current_through` flows
    /// `nodes[0] → nodes[1]`. To get steady-state current, run a
    /// transient long enough to settle.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "inductor"))]
    Inductor {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[a, b]`; `current_through` flows `nodes[0] → nodes[1]`.
        nodes: [String; 2],
        /// Inductance (H): the small-signal value, at zero current.
        inductance: f64,
        /// Core saturation: the inductance falls towards `l_sat` as the
        /// current passes `i_sat`. `None` is a linear inductor.
        #[cfg_attr(
            feature = "serde",
            serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
        )]
        saturation: Option<sindr_devices::inductor::InductorSaturation>,
    },

    /// Diode (Shockley model, silicon unless `model` says otherwise).
    /// `nodes: [anode, cathode]`. Forward current flows from anode → cathode;
    /// positive `voltage_across` corresponds to forward bias.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "diode"))]
    Diode {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[anode, cathode]`.
        nodes: [String; 2],
        /// Junction temperature (K), positive and finite. Default 300.15 K.
        /// Sets IS (SPICE temperature scaling) and the thermal voltage kT/q.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_junction_temperature"))]
        temperature: f64,
        /// Model parameters (IS, N, RS). `None` is the built-in silicon diode,
        /// the same as `Some(DiodeModel::default())`.
        #[cfg_attr(
            feature = "serde",
            serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
        )]
        model: Option<DiodeModel>,
    },

    /// LED. `nodes: [anode, cathode]`. Forward voltage drop depends on
    /// `color` (e.g. `"red"` ≈ 1.8 V, `"blue"` ≈ 3.2 V).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "led"))]
    Led {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[anode, cathode]`.
        nodes: [String; 2],
        /// Emission colour (e.g. `"red"`, `"blue"`); sets the forward voltage drop.
        color: String,
        /// Junction temperature (K), positive and finite. Default 300.15 K.
        /// Sets IS (SPICE temperature scaling) and the thermal voltage kT/q.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_junction_temperature"))]
        temperature: f64,
    },

    /// BJT transistor (3 terminals): Ebers–Moll with Early effect, solved in
    /// DC, transient and AC.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "bjt"))]
    Bjt {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[base, collector, emitter]`.
        nodes: [String; 3], // [base, collector, emitter]
        /// Polarity (NPN or PNP).
        kind: BjtKind,
        /// Forward current gain β (unitless), positive and finite. Default 100.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_bf"))]
        bf: f64,
        /// Junction temperature (K), positive and finite. Default 300.15 K.
        /// Sets IS (SPICE temperature scaling) and the thermal voltage kT/q.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_junction_temperature"))]
        temperature: f64,
        /// Optional parasitic capacitances (Cbe, Cbc). None = no parasitic caps (default).
        #[cfg_attr(
            feature = "serde",
            serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
        )]
        parasitic_caps: Option<BjtParasiticCaps>,
        /// Ebers–Moll parameters besides `bf` (IS, BR, NF, NR, VAF). `None`
        /// is the built-in transistor, the same as `Some(BjtModel::default())`.
        #[cfg_attr(
            feature = "serde",
            serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
        )]
        model: Option<BjtModel>,
    },

    /// MOSFET transistor (3 terminals: gate, drain, source; the body is tied
    /// to the source).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "mosfet"))]
    Mosfet {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[gate, drain, source]`.
        nodes: [String; 3], // [gate, drain, source]
        /// Channel type (NMOS or PMOS).
        kind: MosfetKind,
        /// Model parameters (threshold voltage, transconductance, etc.).
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
        params: MosfetParams,
        /// Optional parasitic capacitances (Cgs, Cgd). None = no parasitic caps (default).
        #[cfg_attr(
            feature = "serde",
            serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
        )]
        parasitic_caps: Option<MosfetParasiticCaps>,
        /// A power MOSFET's body diode, as a SPICE diode card: anode at the
        /// source and cathode at the drain for NMOS, the other way round for
        /// PMOS. It conducts when the drain is pulled past the source, as
        /// in a bridge's freewheeling interval. Every analysis solves it as
        /// a [`CircuitElement::Diode`] with id `<id>.body`, which is where
        /// its current is reported. `None` (default) is no body diode.
        #[cfg_attr(
            feature = "serde",
            serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
        )]
        body_diode: Option<DiodeModel>,
    },

    /// N-channel or P-channel JFET (Shockley square-law model).
    /// nodes: [gate, drain, source]
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "jfet"))]
    Jfet {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[gate, drain, source]`.
        nodes: [String; 3], // [gate, drain, source]
        /// Channel type (N-channel or P-channel).
        kind: JfetKind,
        /// Drain saturation current at Vgs=0 (A). Typical: 1–20 mA.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_jfet_idss"))]
        idss: f64,
        /// Pinch-off voltage (V, negative for N-channel, e.g. -2.0).
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_jfet_vp"))]
        vp: f64,
    },

    /// Voltage-Controlled Voltage Source: V_out = mu * V_control.
    /// nodes: [out+, out-], control_nodes: [ctrl+, ctrl-]
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "vcvs"))]
    Vcvs {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Output terminals `[out+, out-]`.
        nodes: [String; 2],
        /// Sensing terminals `[ctrl+, ctrl-]`.
        control_nodes: [String; 2],
        /// Voltage gain μ (V/V): `V_out = gain * V_control`.
        gain: f64, // mu
    },

    /// Voltage-Controlled Current Source: I_out = gm * V_control.
    /// nodes: [out_from, out_to], control_nodes: [ctrl+, ctrl-]
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "vccs"))]
    Vccs {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Output terminals `[out_from, out_to]`.
        nodes: [String; 2],
        /// Sensing terminals `[ctrl+, ctrl-]`.
        control_nodes: [String; 2],
        /// Transconductance gm (A/V): `I_out = gm * V_control`.
        gm: f64,
    },

    /// Current-Controlled Voltage Source: V_out = rm * I_control.
    /// nodes: [out+, out-], control_source: id of controlling voltage source
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "ccvs"))]
    Ccvs {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Output terminals `[out+, out-]`.
        nodes: [String; 2],
        /// Id of the voltage source whose current is sensed.
        control_source: String,
        /// Transresistance rm (Ω): `V_out = rm * I_control`.
        rm: f64,
    },

    /// Current-Controlled Current Source: I_out = alpha * I_control.
    /// nodes: [out_from, out_to], control_source: id of controlling voltage source
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "cccs"))]
    Cccs {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Output terminals `[out_from, out_to]`.
        nodes: [String; 2],
        /// Id of the voltage source whose current is sensed.
        control_source: String,
        /// Current gain α (A/A): `I_out = alpha * I_control`.
        alpha: f64,
    },

    /// Pushbutton (momentary switch): identical behaviour to Switch.
    /// When closed = true, current flows; when false, open circuit.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "pushbutton"))]
    Pushbutton {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[a, b]`.
        nodes: [String; 2],
        /// When true the button conducts (pressed); when false it is open.
        closed: bool,
    },

    /// Relay: 4-terminal component with a coil and a contact pair.
    /// nodes: [coil+, coil-, contact1, contact2]
    /// Contact closes when |V_coil| >= pickup_voltage. AC and `.tf` take the
    /// contact as open or closed at the DC bias point.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "relay"))]
    Relay {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[coil+, coil-, contact1, contact2]`.
        nodes: [String; 4],
        /// Coil resistance (Ω). Default 500.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_relay_coil_resistance"))]
        coil_resistance: f64,
        /// Coil voltage magnitude at which the contact closes (V).
        pickup_voltage: f64,
        /// Coil inductance in Henry, in series with `coil_resistance` in
        /// transient. 0.0 = purely resistive coil.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
        inductance: f64,
    },

    /// Photoresistor (LDR): resistance varies logarithmically with light.
    /// light_level = 0.0 → ~1 MΩ (dark), 1.0 → ~1 kΩ (bright).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "photoresistor"))]
    Photoresistor {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[a, b]`.
        nodes: [String; 2],
        /// Incident light level, 0.0 (dark, ~1 MΩ) to 1.0 (bright, ~1 kΩ).
        light_level: f64,
    },

    /// Potentiometer: 3-terminal voltage divider.
    /// nodes: [top, wiper, bottom]
    /// position = 0.0 → wiper at top, 1.0 → wiper at bottom.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "potentiometer"))]
    Potentiometer {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[top, wiper, bottom]`.
        nodes: [String; 3],
        /// End-to-end resistance (Ω).
        resistance: f64,
        /// Wiper position, 0.0 (at top) to 1.0 (at bottom).
        position: f64,
    },

    /// Zener diode between two nodes: a silicon diode with SPICE reverse
    /// breakdown, `BV = vz` at `IBV` = 5 mA and 1 Ω of series resistance
    /// (the card `D(IS=1e-14 N=1 RS=1 BV=vz IBV=5m)`), so it holds about
    /// `vz` at a small zener's 5 mA test current and rises 1 V per amp past
    /// it. For another knee, use a [`CircuitElement::Diode`] with a
    /// [`DiodeModel`] setting `bv` and `ibv`.
    /// nodes: [anode, cathode]
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "zener_diode"))]
    ZenerDiode {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[anode, cathode]`.
        nodes: [String; 2],
        /// Reverse breakdown (Zener) voltage (V).
        vz: f64,
        /// Junction temperature (K), positive and finite. Default 300.15 K.
        /// Sets IS (SPICE temperature scaling) and the thermal voltage kT/q.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_junction_temperature"))]
        temperature: f64,
    },

    /// Op-amp, output referred to ground.
    ///
    /// With `model: None` it is the near-ideal VCVS sindr has always used:
    /// gain 1e5, no frequency response, no output resistance, and `v_pos` /
    /// `v_neg` not enforced. With an [`OpAmpModel`] it gets a dominant pole
    /// from the gain-bandwidth product, slew-rate limiting, output
    /// resistance, input offset and bias current, and an output clamped to
    /// `v_pos`/`v_neg`.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "op_amp"))]
    OpAmp {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[in_plus, in_minus, out]`.
        nodes: [String; 3], // [in_plus, in_minus, out]
        /// Positive supply rail (V): the output's upper limit with a
        /// `model`. Default 15.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_v_pos"))]
        v_pos: f64,
        /// Negative supply rail (V): the output's lower limit with a
        /// `model`. Default -15.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_v_neg"))]
        v_neg: f64,
        /// Macromodel parameters; `None` for the near-ideal VCVS.
        #[cfg_attr(
            feature = "serde",
            serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
        )]
        model: Option<OpAmpModel>,
    },

    /// Ideal comparator (same VCVS stamp as OpAmp; output saturates to supply rails).
    /// nodes: [in_plus, in_minus, out]
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "comparator"))]
    Comparator {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[in_plus, in_minus, out]`.
        nodes: [String; 3], // [in_plus, in_minus, out]
        /// Positive supply rail / output high level (V). Default 15.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_v_pos"))]
        v_pos: f64,
        /// Negative supply rail / output low level (V). Default -15.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_v_neg"))]
        v_neg: f64,
    },

    /// Schottky diode: lower forward voltage (~0.3V) than silicon diode.
    /// nodes: [anode, cathode]
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "schottky_diode"))]
    SchottkyDiode {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[anode, cathode]`.
        nodes: [String; 2],
        /// Junction temperature (K), positive and finite. Default 300.15 K.
        /// Sets IS (SPICE temperature scaling) and the thermal voltage kT/q.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_junction_temperature"))]
        temperature: f64,
    },

    /// NTC thermistor: resistance varies with temperature (passive, no NR).
    /// nodes: [n1, n2]
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "thermistor"))]
    Thermistor {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[n1, n2]`.
        nodes: [String; 2],
        /// Temperature in Kelvin, positive and finite. Default: 298.15 K (25°C).
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_temperature"))]
        temperature: f64,
    },

    /// Photodiode: diode + photocurrent source driven by irradiance.
    /// nodes: [anode, cathode]
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "photodiode"))]
    Photodiode {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[anode, cathode]`.
        nodes: [String; 2],
        /// Incident irradiance in W (optical power, not W/m²).
        /// 0.0 = dark, 0.1 = ~50mA photocurrent with default responsivity.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
        irradiance: f64,
        /// Junction temperature (K), positive and finite. Default 300.15 K.
        /// Sets IS (SPICE temperature scaling) and the thermal voltage kT/q.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_junction_temperature"))]
        temperature: f64,
    },

    /// Varactor diode: voltage-dependent junction capacitance.
    /// Open circuit in DC (a 1 TΩ leak); voltage-dependent capacitor in
    /// transient; in AC, its capacitance at the DC bias point.
    /// nodes: [anode, cathode]
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "varactor"))]
    Varactor {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[anode, cathode]`.
        nodes: [String; 2],
        /// Model parameters (zero-bias capacitance, grading, etc.).
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
        params: sindr_devices::varactor::VaractorParams,
    },

    /// IGBT: MOSFET gate control + BJT output characteristics.
    /// Nonlinear element — requires Newton-Raphson iteration.
    /// nodes: [gate, collector, emitter]
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "igbt"))]
    Igbt {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[gate, collector, emitter]`.
        nodes: [String; 3],
        /// Model parameters (threshold voltage, transconductance, etc.).
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
        params: sindr_devices::igbt::IgbtParams,
    },

    /// Ideal transformer with coupled inductors.
    ///
    /// nodes: [p1, q1, p2, q2] where:
    ///   - [p1, q1]: primary winding (+ and - terminals)
    ///   - [p2, q2]: secondary winding (+ and - terminals)
    ///
    /// Coupling: M = k * sqrt(L1 * L2) where k ∈ [0, 1).
    /// k=1 is ideal (no leakage), but mathematically singular — use k<=0.999.
    ///
    /// In DC analysis: both windings stamped as short circuits; the bias point
    /// for AC, `.tf` and `.sens` shorts each with a 0 V source.
    /// In AC: the coupled pair `V = jω·[[L1, M], [M, L2]]·I`.
    /// In transient: coupled-inductor companion with 2 branch current unknowns,
    /// each winding `V = L·dI/dt` plus the mutual term. The windings start at
    /// 0 A; an initial current on a transformer is rejected.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "transformer"))]
    Transformer {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[p1, q1, p2, q2]`: primary `[p1, q1]`, secondary `[p2, q2]`.
        nodes: [String; 4], // [p1, q1, p2, q2]
        /// Primary winding inductance (H).
        l1: f64, // Primary inductance (H)
        /// Secondary winding inductance (H).
        l2: f64, // Secondary inductance (H)
        /// Coupling coefficient (unitless) in `[0, 0.999]`. Default 0.999 (near-ideal).
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_coupling"))]
        k: f64, // Coupling coefficient [0, 0.999]. Default 0.999 (near-ideal).
    },

    /// Fuse between two nodes.
    ///
    /// Intact (blown=false): stamped as 0.001 Ω (1 mΩ) — negligible voltage drop.
    /// Blown (blown=true): stamped as 1e9 Ω — effectively open circuit.
    ///
    /// NOTE: Do NOT use 0 Ω — that would cause a singular MNA matrix.
    /// rating is stored for display purposes only (v1 — no auto-blow logic).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "fuse"))]
    Fuse {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[a, b]`.
        nodes: [String; 2],
        /// Current rating in Amperes (display only — no auto-blow logic in v1).
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_fuse_rating"))]
        rating: f64,
        /// When true, fuse is blown (open circuit). User-settable, like switch.closed.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
        blown: bool,
    },

    /// Linear voltage regulator: holds the output at `voltage` above its
    /// ground pin while it has headroom, and draws its output current plus
    /// its quiescent current from the input.
    ///
    /// Piecewise linear (see `sindr_devices::regulator`): out of headroom
    /// the output follows the input down by the dropout; past the current
    /// limit it holds the current. `model` sets dropout, quiescent current,
    /// current limit and line and load regulation;
    /// `RegulatorParams::lm7805()` and `::ams1117()` are datasheet presets.
    /// Its result is the pass element: `Vin − Vout`, the output current,
    /// and the power it dissipates.
    ///
    /// `nodes: [input, output, gnd]`
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "voltage_regulator"))]
    VoltageRegulator {
        /// Unique component identifier.
        id: String,
        /// Terminals `[input, output, gnd]`.
        nodes: [String; 3], // [input, output, gnd]
        /// Regulated output voltage (V). E.g. 5.0 for a 7805.
        voltage: f64,
        /// Dropout, quiescent current, limit and regulation. `None` is an
        /// ideal regulator that still can't put out more than it gets in.
        #[cfg_attr(
            feature = "serde",
            serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
        )]
        model: Option<sindr_devices::regulator::RegulatorParams>,
    },
}

impl CircuitElement {
    /// Returns a reference to the node array for this component.
    pub fn nodes(&self) -> &[String] { … }

    /// Returns all node names referenced by this component, including control nodes.
    pub fn all_nodes(&self) -> Vec<&String> { … }

    /// Returns the component identifier.
    pub fn id(&self) -> &str { … }

    /// Extra MNA unknowns the element adds after the node voltages: one
    /// branch current for a voltage-type source, two for a transformer
    /// (one per winding), and two for an op-amp with an [`OpAmpModel`]
    /// (its output current, then its internal gain-stage voltage).
    pub fn branch_slots(&self) -> usize { … }

    /// Mutable [`nodes`](Self::nodes), for renaming nets.
    pub fn nodes_mut(&mut self) -> &mut [String] { … }

    /// Mutable [`id`](Self::id), for renaming.
    pub fn id_mut(&mut self) -> &mut String { … }

    /// The control-net pair of a VCVS or VCCS.
    pub fn control_nodes_mut(&mut self) -> Option<&mut [String; 2]> { … }

    /// The controlling source id of a CCVS or CCCS.
    pub fn control_source_mut(&mut self) -> Option<&mut String> { … }
}

/// A circuit: components, nets, and optionally a design hierarchy.
///
/// The top level is a list of [`CircuitElement`]s plus the name of the
/// ground net. Components share a net by referencing the same net-name
/// string. A design can also place [`Block`]s through [`Instance`]s and
/// carry [`Part`] data (reference, symbol, footprint) that the simulator
/// ignores. [`Circuit::flatten`] expands the hierarchy; sindr's analyses
/// do that themselves.
///
/// # Example
///
/// ```
/// use sindr_core::{Circuit, CircuitElement};
///
/// let circuit = Circuit::new(
///     "0",
///     vec![
///         CircuitElement::VoltageSource {
///             id: "V1".into(),
///             nodes: ["n1".into(), "0".into()],
///             voltage: 9.0,
///             waveform: None,
///         },
///         CircuitElement::Resistor {
///             id: "R1".into(),
///             nodes: ["n1".into(), "0".into()],
///             resistance: 1_000.0,
///         },
///     ],
/// );
/// assert!(circuit.is_flat());
/// ```
pub struct Circuit {
    /// Top-level components. Order has no semantic meaning.
    pub components: Vec<CircuitElement>,
    /// Name of the reference (0 V) net. Must match the net string used by
    /// at least one component (typically `"0"` or `"gnd"`). It is the same
    /// net inside every block.
    pub ground_node: String,
    /// Top-level block instances.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")
    )]
    pub instances: Vec<Instance>,
    /// Block definitions, by name.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")
    )]
    pub blocks: BTreeMap<String, Block>,
    /// Part data for top-level components and instances, keyed by their id.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")
    )]
    pub parts: BTreeMap<String, Part>,
    /// Nets visible inside every block under the same name (supply rails),
    /// besides ground. Never prefixed when flattening.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")
    )]
    pub globals: Vec<String>,
}

impl Circuit {
    /// A flat circuit: `components` referencing `ground_node`, no hierarchy.
    pub fn new(ground_node: impl Into<String>, components: Vec<CircuitElement>) -> Self { … }

    /// `true` when there are no instances to expand.
    pub fn is_flat(&self) -> bool { … }

    /// Every net named at the top level: component and instance nodes plus
    /// ground, sorted and without repeats. Nets local to block instances
    /// show up only after [`flatten`](Self::flatten).
    pub fn nets(&self) -> Vec<&str> { … }

    /// Count the number of independent voltage sources in the circuit.
    /// Also counts VCVS, CCVS, OpAmp, and Comparator which need branch currents.
    /// Transformer adds 2 branch current unknowns (one per winding).
    pub fn count_voltage_sources(&self) -> usize { … }

    /// Returns true if the circuit contains any nonlinear elements.
    pub fn has_nonlinear_elements(&self) -> bool { … }

    /// Returns true if the circuit contains any reactive elements (Capacitor, Inductor, or
    /// Relay with inductance > 0, or Transformer, or BJT/MOSFET with non-zero parasitic caps,
    /// or a diode whose model stores charge).
    pub fn has_reactive_elements(&self) -> bool { … }

    /// Returns true if any source has a time-varying waveform.
    pub fn has_waveform_sources(&self) -> bool { … }

    /// Find the branch index for a voltage source by its ID.
    /// Returns None if not found.
    pub fn vsource_branch_index(&self, source_id: &str) -> Option<usize> { … }
}
```

## `sindr-core/src/design.rs`

Design hierarchy and part data: [`Block`], [`Instance`], [`Part`], and
[`Circuit::flatten`].

A [`Block`] is a reusable definition, what `.subckt` is in SPICE. An
[`Instance`] places a block and binds its ports to the caller's nets,
what an `X` line is. Inside a block a net name is a port, ground
([`Circuit::ground_node`]), a global ([`Circuit::globals`]), or local to
each instance.

Flattening names things the way the SPICE parser always has: elements
and local nets get the instance path joined with `.` (`x1.x2.r1`,
`x1.mid`), ports become the caller's net, and ground and globals are
never prefixed.

```
use sindr_core::{Block, Circuit, CircuitElement, Instance};

let divider = Block {
    ports: vec!["top".into(), "out".into()],
    components: vec![
        CircuitElement::Resistor { id: "R1".into(), nodes: ["top".into(), "out".into()], resistance: 1e3 },
        CircuitElement::Resistor { id: "R2".into(), nodes: ["out".into(), "0".into()], resistance: 1e3 },
    ],
    ..Block::default()
};
let mut circuit = Circuit::new(
    "0",
    vec![CircuitElement::VoltageSource { id: "V1".into(), nodes: ["in".into(), "0".into()], voltage: 10.0, waveform: None }],
);
circuit.blocks.insert("divider".into(), divider);
circuit.instances.push(Instance::new("X1", "divider", ["in", "mid"]));

let flat = circuit.flatten().unwrap();
assert!(flat.is_flat());
assert_eq!(flat.components[1].id(), "X1.R1");
assert_eq!(flat.components[2].nodes(), ["mid", "0"]);
```

```rust
/// Separator between instance-path segments in flattened names.
pub const PATH_SEPARATOR: char = '.';

/// A reusable block definition: what `.subckt` is in SPICE.
pub struct Block {
    /// Port nets, in the order [`Instance::nodes`] binds them.
    pub ports: Vec<String>,
    /// Components inside the block, named in the block's own scope.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub components: Vec<CircuitElement>,
    /// Instances of other blocks placed inside this one.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")
    )]
    pub instances: Vec<Instance>,
    /// Part data for the block's components and instances, keyed by id.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")
    )]
    pub parts: BTreeMap<String, Part>,
}

/// One placement of a [`Block`]: what an `X` line is in SPICE.
pub struct Instance {
    /// Instance id, unique in its scope (`"X1"`). Prefixes everything inside
    /// it when flattened.
    pub id: String,
    /// Name of the block it places, a key of [`Circuit::blocks`].
    pub block: String,
    /// The caller's nets, bound to [`Block::ports`] by position.
    pub nodes: Vec<String>,
}

impl Instance {
    /// An instance of `block` with `nodes` bound to its ports in order.
    pub fn new<S: Into<String>>(
        id: impl Into<String>,
        block: impl Into<String>,
        nodes: impl IntoIterator<Item = S>,
    ) -> Self { … }
}

/// Part data for a component or instance: what a schematic or BOM needs.
/// The simulator ignores it.
pub struct Part {
    /// Reference designator (`"R1"`). `None` means the element id is the
    /// reference.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub reference: Option<String>,
    /// Display value (`"10k"`, `"BC547"`).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub value: Option<String>,
    /// Schematic symbol, in whatever form the design tool uses
    /// (`"Device:R"`).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub symbol: Option<String>,
    /// PCB footprint (`"Resistor_SMD:R_0603_1608Metric"`).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub footprint: Option<String>,
    /// Any other fields: manufacturer, MPN, tolerance, …
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty"))]
    pub fields: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    /// Absolute maximum ratings from the datasheet. `sindr::check_ratings`
    /// compares a simulation against them.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Ratings::is_empty"))]
    pub ratings: Ratings,
    /// How the part sheds heat. When set, the solver heats its junction by
    /// the power it dissipates; see [`Thermal`].
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub thermal: Option<Thermal>,
}

/// A part's thermal path to ambient, for self-heating.
///
/// With it, the part's junction runs at `ambient + P·Rθ` in DC, or follows
/// `Cθ·dT/dt = P − (T − ambient)/Rθ` in a transient, and the solver feeds
/// that temperature back into the device (IS and kT/q for diodes, LEDs and
/// BJTs; the thermistor's resistance). The element's own `temperature`
/// field is then ignored.
///
/// Rθ is [`rth_jc`](Self::rth_jc) + [`rth_ca`](Self::rth_ca) when both are
/// set (a part on a heatsink), otherwise [`rth_ja`](Self::rth_ja).
pub struct Thermal {
    /// Junction to ambient (K/W), the datasheet's Rθja for the part on its
    /// own.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub rth_ja: Option<f64>,
    /// Junction to case (K/W).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub rth_jc: Option<f64>,
    /// Case to ambient through what the part is mounted on: interface pad
    /// plus heatsink (K/W).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub rth_ca: Option<f64>,
    /// Thermal capacitance (J/K). `None` in a transient means the junction
    /// follows its power with no lag.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub cth: Option<f64>,
    /// Ambient temperature (K). Default 300.15 K (27 °C).
    pub ambient: f64,
}

impl Thermal {
    /// A free-standing part: junction to ambient `rth_ja` (K/W).
    pub fn junction_to_ambient(rth_ja: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// A part on a heatsink: junction to case `rth_jc` plus case to ambient
    /// `rth_ca` (K/W).
    pub fn on_heatsink(rth_jc: f64, rth_ca: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// The thermal resistance from junction to ambient (K/W) the solver
    /// uses, or `None` when neither path is set.
    pub fn resistance(&self) -> Option<f64> { … }
}

/// Absolute maximum ratings: the datasheet limits a part must never pass.
///
/// Every limit is a magnitude in SI units and `None` when unknown. A rating
/// a part needs but doesn't have is reported as unverified, never as a
/// pass. Which ratings a component needs depends on its kind; see
/// `sindr::ratings`.
pub struct Ratings {
    /// Power dissipation (W).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub power: Option<f64>,
    /// Voltage across the part (V): a capacitor's rated voltage, a
    /// resistor's working voltage.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub voltage: Option<f64>,
    /// Current through the part (A): an inductor's saturation current.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub current: Option<f64>,
    /// Diode reverse voltage, cathode above anode (V).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub reverse_voltage: Option<f64>,
    /// Diode forward current, anode to cathode (A).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub forward_current: Option<f64>,
    /// BJT or IGBT collector–emitter voltage, `|Vce|` (V).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub vce: Option<f64>,
    /// BJT collector–base voltage, `|Vcb|` (V).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub vcb: Option<f64>,
    /// BJT emitter–base voltage, `|Veb|` (V).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub veb: Option<f64>,
    /// BJT or IGBT collector current, `|Ic|` (A).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub ic: Option<f64>,
    /// MOSFET or JFET drain–source voltage, `|Vds|` (V).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub vds: Option<f64>,
    /// MOSFET or JFET gate–source voltage, `|Vgs|`; an IGBT's gate–emitter
    /// voltage (V).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub vgs: Option<f64>,
    /// MOSFET or JFET drain current, `|Id|` (A).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub id: Option<f64>,
    /// Maximum junction temperature (K): 423.15 K for a 150 °C part. Checked
    /// against the junction temperature self-heating reports, so it needs
    /// [`Part::thermal`].
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub tj_max: Option<f64>,
}

impl Ratings {
    /// `true` when no limit is set.
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool { … }
}

/// Why a design can't be flattened.
pub enum DesignError {
    /// An instance names a block that isn't in [`Circuit::blocks`].
    #[error("instance `{instance}` places block `{block}`, which is not defined")]
    UnknownBlock {
        /// Full path of the instance (`x1.x2`).
        instance: String,
        /// The missing block.
        block: String,
    },
    /// An instance binds a different number of nets than the block has ports.
    #[error("instance `{instance}` connects {got} nets, but block `{block}` has {expected} ports")]
    PortCount {
        /// Full path of the instance.
        instance: String,
        /// The block it places.
        block: String,
        /// Ports the block declares.
        expected: usize,
        /// Nets the instance binds.
        got: usize,
    },
    /// A block places itself, directly or through other blocks.
    #[error("instance `{instance}` places block `{block}` inside itself")]
    RecursiveBlock {
        /// Full path of the instance that closes the loop.
        instance: String,
        /// The block that recurses.
        block: String,
    },
    /// Two components or instances in one scope share an id.
    #[error("id `{id}` is used twice in {scope}")]
    DuplicateId {
        /// The repeated id.
        id: String,
        /// `"the top level"` or `"block `name`"`.
        scope: String,
    },
}

impl Circuit {
    /// Expand every instance into a flat circuit with no instances or
    /// blocks. Names follow the module docs; `parts` keys get the same
    /// prefix as their element, and `globals` carry over.
    ///
    /// Top-level components come first, then each instance's expansion in
    /// order, depth-first.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`DesignError`] for an unknown block, a port-count mismatch, a
    /// recursive block, or a repeated id in one scope.
    pub fn flatten(&self) -> Result<Circuit, DesignError> { … }

    /// [`flatten`](Self::flatten), borrowing `self` when it is already flat.
    pub fn flattened(&self) -> Result<Cow<'_, Circuit>, DesignError> { … }
}
```

## `sindr-core/src/lib.rs`

The circuit and design data model behind
[`sindr`](https://crates.io/crates/sindr), without the solver.

- [`circuit`]: [`Circuit`] and every [`CircuitElement`] sindr simulates
- [`design`]: hierarchy ([`Block`], [`Instance`]), part data ([`Part`])
  and [`Circuit::flatten`]
- [`waveform`]: time-varying source [`Waveform`]s

The only dependencies are `sindr-devices` (device parameter types),
`thiserror` and, behind the default `serde` feature, `serde`. Design
tools can build and exchange circuits with this crate alone; `sindr`
re-exports all of it and simulates them.

```
use sindr_core::{Circuit, CircuitElement, Part};

let mut circuit = Circuit::new(
    "0",
    vec![CircuitElement::Resistor {
        id: "R1".into(),
        nodes: ["in".into(), "0".into()],
        resistance: 10e3,
    }],
);
circuit.parts.insert(
    "R1".into(),
    Part { value: Some("10k".into()), footprint: Some("R_0603".into()), ..Part::default() },
);
assert_eq!(circuit.nets(), ["0", "in"]);
```

```rust
pub mod circuit;

pub mod design;

pub mod waveform;

pub use circuit:: { … }

pub use design::{Block, DesignError, Instance, Part, Ratings, Thermal};

pub use waveform::Waveform;
```

## `sindr-core/src/waveform.rs`

Time-varying waveform definitions for voltage/current sources.

Each waveform variant implements `evaluate(t)` returning the instantaneous
value at time `t`. When attached to a VoltageSource or CurrentSource via
`waveform: Some(w)`, the source value at each transient timestep becomes
`dc_offset + w.evaluate(t)` (where dc_offset is the existing `voltage`/`current` field),
evaluated at the step's end time. Transient snapshots report that value as
the source's voltage or current. A step that ends on a jump (a square, PWM
or zero-rise pulse edge) sees the value just before it; the next step
starts from the value after.

```rust
/// A time-varying waveform.
pub enum Waveform {
    /// Sinusoidal: amplitude * sin(2*pi*frequency*t + phase) + offset
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "sine"))]
    Sine {
        /// Peak amplitude (V or A).
        amplitude: f64,
        /// Frequency (Hz).
        frequency: f64,
        /// DC offset added to the sine (V or A). Default 0.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
        offset: f64,
        /// Phase offset (radians). Default 0.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
        phase: f64, // radians
    },

    /// SPICE-compatible pulse waveform.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "pulse"))]
    Pulse {
        /// Initial (low) value (V or A).
        v1: f64, // initial value
        /// Pulsed (high) value (V or A).
        v2: f64, // pulsed value
        /// Delay before the first pulse (s). Default 0.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
        delay: f64, // delay before first pulse (s)
        /// Rise time from `v1` to `v2` (s).
        rise_time: f64, // rise time (s)
        /// Fall time from `v2` back to `v1` (s).
        fall_time: f64, // fall time (s)
        /// Width of the high portion of the pulse (s).
        pulse_width: f64, // pulse width (s)
        /// Repetition period (s). Zero, negative or non-finite means a
        /// single pulse, as SPICE reads a zero period.
        period: f64, // period (s)
    },

    /// Square wave with configurable duty cycle.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "square"))]
    Square {
        /// Peak amplitude about the offset (V or A).
        amplitude: f64,
        /// Frequency (Hz).
        frequency: f64,
        /// DC offset added to the wave (V or A). Default 0.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
        offset: f64,
        /// Duty cycle (fraction high), 0.0 to 1.0. Default 0.5.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_duty"))]
        duty: f64, // 0.0 to 1.0, default 0.5
    },

    /// Triangle wave.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "triangle"))]
    Triangle {
        /// Peak amplitude about the offset (V or A).
        amplitude: f64,
        /// Frequency (Hz).
        frequency: f64,
        /// DC offset added to the wave (V or A). Default 0.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
        offset: f64,
    },

    /// PWM (pulse width modulation) — square wave with variable duty.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "pwm"))]
    Pwm {
        /// High-level amplitude above the offset (V or A).
        amplitude: f64,
        /// Frequency (Hz).
        frequency: f64,
        /// Duty cycle (fraction high), 0.0 to 1.0.
        duty: f64, // 0.0 to 1.0
        /// DC offset (low level) (V or A). Default 0.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
        offset: f64,
    },

    /// Piecewise-linear waveform. `points` is a list of `(t, value)`
    /// breakpoints sorted by `t`. Values are linearly interpolated between
    /// adjacent points; for `t < points[0].0` the first value is held, and
    /// for `t > points.last().0` the last value is held. An empty list
    /// evaluates to `0.0` everywhere.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "pwl"))]
    Pwl {
        /// Breakpoints as `(time in s, value)` pairs sorted by time. The
        /// value is V or A, matching the source it drives.
        points: Vec<(f64, f64)>,
    },
}

/// Most breakpoints [`Waveform::breakpoints`] returns.
pub const MAX_BREAKPOINTS: usize = 10_000_000;

impl Waveform {
    /// The waveform's value at time `t` (s): volts on a voltage source,
    /// amperes on a current source.
    pub fn evaluate(&self, t: f64) -> f64 { … }

    /// Times in `(0, t_end)` (s) where this waveform has a corner or a jump:
    /// pulse edges, square/PWM transitions, triangle peaks, PWL points. A sine
    /// has none. Sorted; at most [`MAX_BREAKPOINTS`] of them.
    ///
    /// The transient stepper lands a step exactly on each one, so a fast
    /// edge between two steps isn't stepped over.
    ///
    /// ```
    /// use sindr_core::Waveform;
    ///
    /// let pulse = Waveform::Pulse {
    ///     v1: 0.0, v2: 5.0, delay: 1e-3, rise_time: 1e-9, fall_time: 1e-9,
    ///     pulse_width: 2e-3, period: 10e-3,
    /// };
    /// assert_eq!(pulse.breakpoints(5e-3), vec![1e-3, 1e-3 + 1e-9, 3e-3 + 1e-9, 3e-3 + 2e-9]);
    /// ```
    pub fn breakpoints(&self, t_end: f64) -> Vec<f64> { … }

    /// [`Self::breakpoints`], and whether some were dropped to keep to
    /// [`MAX_BREAKPOINTS`].
    pub fn capped_breakpoints(&self, t_end: f64) -> (Vec<f64>, bool) { … }

    /// Return the period of this waveform in seconds, if periodic. `None`
    /// for a single pulse (period zero, negative or non-finite), PWL, and a
    /// frequency that isn't positive.
    pub fn period(&self) -> Option<f64> { … }
}
```


# Public API of `sindr-devices`

## `sindr-devices/src/battery.rs`

Equivalent-circuit battery: open-circuit voltage by state of charge,
series resistance and an optional RC pair.

```text
 +  ──[ R0 ]──┬──[ R1 ]──┬──(OCV(SoC))──  −
              └──[ C1 ]──┘
```

The terminal voltage is `OCV(SoC) − R0·i − v1`, with `i` the discharge
current (out of the positive terminal) and `v1` the RC pair's voltage,
`C1·dv1/dt = i − v1/R1`. The pair gives the slow sag and recovery after
a load step. State of charge falls as `dSoC/dt = −i/(3600·capacity)`.

Aging, temperature and current-dependent capacity (Peukert) are not
modelled.

```rust
/// The RC pair: the polarisation that makes a loaded cell sag over seconds
/// and recover after the load goes.
pub struct BatteryRc {
    /// Polarisation resistance (Ω).
    pub r: f64,
    /// Polarisation capacitance (F).
    pub c: f64,
}

/// A battery's equivalent circuit.
pub struct BatteryParams {
    /// Capacity (Ah): the charge from full (SoC 1) to empty (SoC 0).
    pub capacity: f64,
    /// Open-circuit (rest) voltage against state of charge: `(SoC, volts)`
    /// pairs with SoC rising from 0 to 1, read by linear interpolation.
    pub ocv: Vec<(f64, f64)>,
    /// Series (ohmic) resistance (Ω), positive.
    pub r_series: f64,
    /// Optional RC pair for the slow part of the sag.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
    )]
    pub rc: Option<BatteryRc>,
}

impl BatteryParams {
    /// A cell with a flat `volts` at every state of charge.
    pub fn constant(volts: f64, capacity: f64, r_series: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// A single lithium-ion or lithium-polymer cell: a typical rest-voltage
    /// curve, 3.27 V empty to 4.20 V full (3.84 V at half charge), with the
    /// capacity (Ah) and series resistance (Ω) of the part. A small pouch
    /// cell is around 0.1–0.3 Ω, an 18650 around 0.03–0.05 Ω.
    pub fn lithium_ion(capacity: f64, r_series: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// A CR2032-class lithium coin cell: 225 mAh, about 3.0 V for most of
    /// its life and falling off over the last tenth, with 15 Ω series
    /// resistance and a 25 Ω, 0.2 F pulse-recovery pair. Approximate,
    /// from typical published discharge curves; a coin cell's resistance
    /// rises steeply as it empties and in the cold, which isn't modelled.
    pub fn cr2032() -> Self { … }
}

/// Open-circuit voltage (V) at state of charge `soc`, interpolated along
/// the curve. Outside 0..1 it holds the end values.
pub fn open_circuit_voltage(soc: f64, params: &BatteryParams) -> f64 { … }

/// The resistance (Ω) a battery shows at DC: `R0`, plus `R1` once the RC
/// pair has settled.
pub fn dc_resistance(params: &BatteryParams) -> f64 { … }

/// State of charge after `amp_hours` (Ah) is drawn from `soc`.
pub fn discharged(soc: f64, amp_hours: f64, params: &BatteryParams) -> f64 { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/bjt.rs`

BJT (Bipolar Junction Transistor) device model.

Ebers–Moll companion model with Early voltage. Produces a 3×3 conductance
/ current contribution that an MNA solver stamps for [base, collector,
emitter] terminals at each Newton–Raphson iteration.

Both NPN and PNP are supported via [`BjtKind`]; the PNP case mirrors NPN
through sign conventions on `vbe` and `vbc`.

```rust
/// BJT polarity.
pub enum BjtKind {
    /// NPN (electrons are majority carriers in base region).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "npn"))]
    Npn,
    /// PNP (holes are majority carriers in base region).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "pnp"))]
    Pnp,
}

/// Operating region of a BJT — useful for diagnostics and circuit
/// classification (amplifier biased "active", switch in "saturation", …).
pub enum BjtRegion {
    /// Both junctions reverse-biased — negligible currents.
    Cutoff,
    /// Forward-active: BE forward-biased, BC reverse-biased. Linear amplifier region.
    Active,
    /// Both junctions forward-biased — output voltage clamped near `VCE_sat`.
    Saturation,
}

impl BjtRegion {
    /// Lowercase string label for the region (`"cutoff"`, `"active"`, `"saturation"`).
    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str { … }
}

/// Ebers–Moll model parameters for a BJT.
pub struct BjtParams {
    /// Saturation current (A).
    pub is: f64, // Saturation current (A)
    /// Forward current gain (unitless).
    pub bf: f64, // Forward current gain
    /// Forward emission coefficient (unitless).
    pub nf: f64, // Forward emission coefficient
    /// Reverse current gain (unitless).
    pub br: f64, // Reverse current gain
    /// Reverse emission coefficient (unitless).
    pub nr: f64, // Reverse emission coefficient
    /// Forward Early voltage (V). 0.0 = infinite (no Early effect).
    pub vaf: f64, // Forward Early voltage (V). 0.0 = infinite (no Early effect).
    /// Reverse Early voltage (V). 0.0 = infinite.
    pub var: f64, // Reverse Early voltage (V). 0.0 = infinite.
    /// Junction temperature (K). Default 300.15 K = 27°C. Sets the thermal
    /// voltage [`BjtParams::vt`]; `is` is used as given.
    pub temperature: f64, // Junction temperature (K). Default 300.15 K = 27°C.
}

impl BjtParams {
    /// Thermal voltage kT/q (V) at the junction temperature.
    pub fn vt(&self) -> f64 { … }

    /// Construct default Ebers–Moll parameters for the given forward gain `bf`.
    pub fn new(bf: f64) -> Self { … }
}

/// Companion model output for one NR iteration.
/// Contains conductances and equivalent currents for MNA stamping.
pub struct BjtCompanion {
    /// B–E forward junction conductance (S).
    pub g_be: f64, // B-E forward junction conductance
    /// B–C reverse junction conductance (S).
    pub g_bc: f64, // B-C reverse junction conductance
    /// Early-voltage output conductance between C and E (S).
    pub g_ce: f64, // Early voltage output conductance between C and E
    /// Collector current at the operating point (A), into the collector, in
    /// the NPN frame: a PNP caller negates it for the physical current.
    pub ic: f64, // collector current at operating point
    /// Base current at the operating point (A), into the base, NPN frame.
    pub ib: f64, // base current at operating point
    /// B–E junction voltage at the operating point (V), for RHS computation.
    pub vbe: f64, // junction voltage (for RHS computation)
    /// B–C junction voltage at the operating point (V), for RHS computation.
    pub vbc: f64, // junction voltage (for RHS computation)
}

/// Evaluate the Ebers–Moll transport model at junction voltages `vbe`/`vbc`
/// (V, sign-adjusted for PNP by the caller), returning the linearised
/// [`BjtCompanion`] for MNA stamping.
///
/// `g_be` and `g_bc` are the exact slopes of the junction currents, with no
/// cap: overshoot is left to the solver's junction voltage limiting. For the
/// full terminal Jacobian, Early effect included, use
/// [`bjt_terminal_jacobian`].
pub fn bjt_companion(vbe: f64, vbc: f64, params: &BjtParams) -> BjtCompanion { … }

/// Base and collector currents `(ib, ic)` (A), each into its terminal, at
/// junction voltages `vbe`/`vbc` (V). Both are in the NPN frame: for a PNP,
/// pass the negated junction voltages and negate the currents. Includes the
/// Early effect the DC solve applies: `ic = i_tr + |i_tr|/VAF · vce` with
/// `vce = vbe − vbc`.
///
/// This is the large-signal model that [`bjt_terminal_jacobian`]
/// differentiates. The emitter current is `−(ib + ic)`.
pub fn bjt_terminal_currents(vbe: f64, vbc: f64, params: &BjtParams) -> (f64, f64) { … }

/// Exact small-signal Jacobian of the BJT terminal currents with respect to
/// the junction voltages, at one operating point.
///
/// These are the true derivatives of [`bjt_terminal_currents`], Early effect
/// included, valid in every region (cutoff, forward-active, saturation,
/// reverse-active). The DC stamp and AC analysis both use them.
///
/// In terms of the node voltages, with `vbe = vb − ve` and `vbc = vb − vc`:
/// `∂I/∂vb = ∂I/∂vbe + ∂I/∂vbc`, `∂I/∂vc = −∂I/∂vbc`, `∂I/∂ve = −∂I/∂vbe`.
/// These entries are the same for NPN and PNP: the polarity sign cancels.
pub struct BjtJacobian {
    /// ∂Ib/∂Vbe (S).
    pub dib_dvbe: f64,
    /// ∂Ib/∂Vbc (S).
    pub dib_dvbc: f64,
    /// ∂Ic/∂Vbe (S).
    pub dic_dvbe: f64,
    /// ∂Ic/∂Vbc (S).
    pub dic_dvbc: f64,
}

impl BjtJacobian {
    /// The 3×3 terminal conductance matrix `∂(Ib, Ic, Ie)/∂(Vb, Vc, Ve)`,
    /// rows and columns ordered [base, collector, emitter]. Rows and columns
    /// each sum to zero (KCL and invariance to a common-mode shift).
    pub fn terminal_matrix(&self) -> [[f64; 3]; 3] { … }
}

/// Evaluate the exact terminal Jacobian of [`bjt_terminal_currents`] at
/// junction voltages `vbe`/`vbc` (V, sign-adjusted for PNP).
pub fn bjt_terminal_jacobian(vbe: f64, vbc: f64, params: &BjtParams) -> BjtJacobian { … }

/// Detect operating region from junction voltages.
pub fn detect_region(vbe: f64, vbc: f64) -> BjtRegion { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/diode.rs`

Diode model: Shockley equation, companion model, voltage limiting.

Provides the mathematical foundation for Newton-Raphson simulation
of diodes and LEDs. Each NR iteration linearizes the diode at its
current operating point into a companion conductance + current source.

```rust
/// Boltzmann constant over the elementary charge, k/q (V/K).
pub const K_OVER_Q: f64 = 8.617_333_262e-5;

/// Nominal temperature (K) the device parameters are given at: 27 °C.
pub const T_NOM: f64 = 300.15;

/// Thermal voltage kT/q at the nominal temperature [`T_NOM`] (V).
pub const V_T: f64 = K_OVER_Q * T_NOM;

/// Thermal voltage kT/q (V) at temperature `t` (K).
pub fn thermal_voltage(t: f64) -> f64 { … }

/// Minimum conductance shunt to prevent singular Jacobian in reverse bias.
pub const GMIN: f64 = 1e-12;

/// Diode parameters (Shockley model).
pub struct DiodeParams {
    /// Saturation current (A).
    pub is: f64,
    /// Emission coefficient (dimensionless).
    pub n: f64,
    /// Series resistance (Ω). Default 0.0 — no effect on existing models.
    pub rs: f64,
    /// Junction temperature (K). Default 300.15 K = 27°C. Sets the thermal
    /// voltage [`DiodeParams::vt`]; `is` is used as given, so scale it with
    /// [`temperature_scale_is`] for a junction away from [`T_NOM`].
    pub temperature: f64,
    /// Reverse breakdown (SPICE `BV`/`IBV`). `None`: the junction never
    /// breaks down, as in SPICE without `BV`.
    pub breakdown: Option<Breakdown>,
}

/// Reverse breakdown of a diode, as a SPICE card's `BV` and `IBV` give it.
///
/// Breakdown adds `−IS·exp(−(v_j + xbv)/(N·V_T))` to the junction current,
/// with `xbv` fitted as ngspice fits it: the current at `v_j = −bv` is
/// `−ibv`, less about `IS·bv/V_T` that ngspice's fit carries. Away from the
/// knee this is the ngspice current to within `IS`.
pub struct Breakdown {
    /// Breakdown voltage BV (V), positive.
    pub bv: f64,
    /// Current at `−bv`, IBV (A), positive. SPICE's default is 1 mA.
    pub ibv: f64,
}

impl DiodeParams {
    /// Thermal voltage kT/q (V) at the junction temperature.
    pub fn vt(&self) -> f64 { … }

    /// Standard silicon diode: IS = 1e-14 A, N = 1.0.
    pub fn silicon() -> Self { … }

    /// LED with a given forward voltage (V) at 20 mA.
    ///
    /// IS is derived from the Shockley equation: IS = 0.020 / (exp(Vf / (N * VT)) - 1)
    /// with N = 2.0 (typical LED emission coefficient).
    pub fn led(forward_voltage: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// LED parameters by colour name.
    ///
    /// Maps common LED colours to their typical forward voltage.
    pub fn for_led_color(color: &str) -> Self { … }
}

/// Scale saturation current IS for junction temperature.
///
/// IS(T) = IS(T0) * (T/T0)^(XTI/N) * exp(Eg / (N * k/q) * (1/T0 - 1/T))
///
/// This is the SPICE formula. For a BJT, SPICE scales IS with N = 1.
///
/// Arguments:
/// - `is_t0`: IS at reference temperature T0 (A)
/// - `t`: Junction temperature (K)
/// - `t0`: Reference temperature (K), typically [`T_NOM`]
/// - `eg`: Bandgap energy (eV): 1.11 for Si, 0.69 for Ge, 1.42 for GaAs
/// - `xti`: Temperature exponent: SPICE's default is 3.0 for diodes and BJTs
/// - `n`: Emission coefficient (1.0 for a BJT)
pub fn temperature_scale_is(is_t0: f64, t: f64, t0: f64, eg: f64, xti: f64, n: f64) -> f64 { … }

/// Compute the companion model (linearised) at operating point `v_d`.
///
/// Returns `(g_d, i_eq)` where:
/// - `g_d` is the companion conductance (dI/dV at v_d), floored at [`GMIN`]
/// - `i_eq` is the companion current source (I_d - g_d * v_d)
///
/// `i_eq` is built from the same floored `g_d`, so `g_d * v_d + i_eq` is
/// always the diode current: the floor shapes the Newton steps in deep
/// reverse bias without adding a GMIN leakage to the converged current.
///
/// These stamp into MNA exactly like a resistor (g_d) and current source (i_eq).
///
/// When `params.rs > 0`, `v_d` is the terminal voltage across junction and
/// series resistance together. The junction voltage is solved from
/// `I = IS * (exp((v_d - I*RS) / (N*V_T)) - 1)`, with V_T at
/// `params.temperature`, and the terminal conductance `g_j / (1 + RS*g_j)`
/// is returned, so `g_d * v_d + i_eq` is the terminal current at `v_d`.
///
/// Units and signs: `v_d` is anode − cathode (V), `g_d` is in S and `i_eq`
/// in A, both for current flowing anode → cathode.
pub fn diode_companion(v_d: f64, params: &DiodeParams) -> (f64, f64) { … }

/// Compute the diode current (A, anode → cathode) at terminal voltage
/// `v_d` (V, anode − cathode), including the drop across `params.rs`.
pub fn diode_current(v_d: f64, params: &DiodeParams) -> f64 { … }

/// Current (A) and conductance (S) of the junction itself at junction
/// voltage `v_j`: Shockley, plus the breakdown branch when `params` has one.
pub fn junction_current(v_j: f64, params: &DiodeParams) -> (f64, f64) { … }

/// Charge-storage parameters of a junction, as a SPICE diode card's `CJO`,
/// `VJ`, `M`, `FC` and `TT` give them. The default stores no charge.
pub struct JunctionCharge {
    /// Zero-bias depletion capacitance CJO (F). Default 0.
    pub cjo: f64,
    /// Junction potential VJ (V). Default 1.
    pub vj: f64,
    /// Grading coefficient M, in `[0, 1)`. Default 0.5.
    pub m: f64,
    /// Forward-bias depletion coefficient FC, in `[0, 1)`: above `FC·VJ` the
    /// depletion capacitance is continued linearly. Default 0.5.
    pub fc: f64,
    /// Transit time TT (s): the diffusion charge is `TT·I_d`. Default 0.
    pub tt: f64,
}

impl JunctionCharge {
    /// Whether the junction stores any charge at all.
    pub fn is_none(&self) -> bool { … }

    /// Stored charge (C) and capacitance dQ/dV (F) at junction voltage `v`
    /// (V), carrying current `i_d` (A) with conductance `g_d` (S).
    ///
    /// The SPICE junction charge: depletion `CJO·VJ·(1 − (1 − v/VJ)^(1−M))/(1−M)`
    /// up to `FC·VJ`, continued with a linear capacitance above it so it
    /// stays finite in forward bias, plus diffusion `TT·I_d`.
    pub fn charge(&self, v: f64, i_d: f64, g_d: f64) -> (f64, f64) { … }
}

/// The junction behind RS at terminal voltage `v_d` (V): its conductance
/// `g_j` (S) and capacitance `c_j` (F). In AC the diode is RS in series with
/// `g_j + jωC_j`.
pub fn junction_small_signal(
    v_d: f64,
    params: &DiodeParams,
    charge: &JunctionCharge,
) -> (f64, f64) { … }

/// Stored charge (C) and its derivative with respect to the terminal
/// voltage (F) of a diode at terminal voltage `v_d` (V, anode − cathode).
///
/// The charge is the junction's at the junction voltage the diode current
/// sets across RS. The drop the charging current itself makes across RS is
/// left out, so with RS > 0 the charge sits across the terminals.
pub fn diode_charge(v_d: f64, params: &DiodeParams, charge: &JunctionCharge) -> (f64, f64) { … }

/// Critical voltage for voltage limiting.
///
/// V_crit = N * V_T * ln(N * V_T / (sqrt(2) * IS)), with `vt` the thermal
/// voltage at the junction temperature.
pub fn critical_voltage(is: f64, n: f64, vt: f64) -> f64 { … }

/// SPICE-style voltage limiting to prevent NR overshoot.
///
/// If the proposed new voltage `v_new` exceeds V_crit above `v_old`,
/// the step is compressed logarithmically to keep the exponential
/// in the Shockley equation from overflowing. `vt` is the thermal voltage at
/// the junction temperature.
pub fn limit_voltage(v_new: f64, v_old: f64, v_crit: f64, n: f64, vt: f64) -> f64 { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/igbt.rs`

IGBT (Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistor) simplified model.

An IGBT combines MOSFET gate control with BJT output characteristics.
This educational model uses the MOSFET Level-1 square law for the
collector current, and blocks reverse collector-emitter voltage.

Nodes: [gate, collector, emitter] — same ordering convention as BJT.
Gate controls current like a MOSFET; collector/emitter behave like BJT.

Simplified model is appropriate for educational simulation.
Full IGBT models (IGBTv3) have 20+ parameters — out of scope.

```rust
/// IGBT parameters (simplified model).
pub struct IgbtParams {
    /// Gate threshold voltage (V). Typical: 4.0–6.0 V.
    pub vth: f64,
    /// Transconductance parameter (A/V²). Typical: 5.0.
    pub k: f64,
    /// On-state collector-emitter saturation voltage (V). Typical: 2.0.
    ///
    /// Not used by the current I–V model: the collector current follows the
    /// square law alone. Kept so existing circuits still deserialize.
    pub vce_sat: f64,
}

/// IGBT companion model output.
pub struct IgbtCompanion {
    /// Transconductance ∂Ids/∂Vge (S).
    pub gm: f64,
    /// Output conductance ∂Ids/∂Vce (S): zero in saturation and cutoff.
    pub g_ce: f64,
    /// Collector current at the operating point (A), collector → emitter.
    pub ids: f64,
    /// Companion current source value for MNA stamping (A), collector →
    /// emitter: `ids − gm·vge − g_ce·vce`.
    pub i_eq: f64,
}

/// Evaluate IGBT companion model at gate-emitter voltage `vge` and
/// collector-emitter voltage `vce`.
///
/// Collector current (MOSFET Level-1), with `vov = vge − vth`:
/// - cutoff (`vov ≤ 0`) or reverse (`vce ≤ 0`): 0
/// - saturation (`vce ≥ vov`): `K/2 · vov²`
/// - triode (`0 < vce < vov`): `K · (vov − vce/2) · vce`
///
/// `gm` and `g_ce` are the exact partial derivatives of that current, so the
/// linearisation `Ic ≈ gm·vge + g_ce·vce + i_eq` is a Newton step. The stamp
/// puts `gm` in as a gate-controlled current source and `g_ce` as a C–E
/// conductance.
pub fn igbt_companion(vge: f64, vce: f64, params: &IgbtParams) -> IgbtCompanion { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/inductor.rs`

Saturating inductor core: inductance that falls as the current rises.

A ferrite or iron core holds its initial inductance `L0` at small
currents and falls towards an air-core floor `l_sat` once the flux
approaches saturation. The flux linkage is

```text
λ(i) = l_sat·i + (L0 − l_sat)·i_sat·tanh(i / i_sat)
L(i) = dλ/di = l_sat + (L0 − l_sat)·sech²(i / i_sat)
```

so L is `L0` at zero current, `l_sat + 0.42·(L0 − l_sat)` at `i_sat`
and `l_sat + 0.07·(L0 − l_sat)` at `2·i_sat`. The curve is
single-valued: no hysteresis, remanence or core loss. Put a resistor in
series or parallel for loss.

A simulator integrates the flux (`v = dλ/dt`) and recovers the current
with [`current_from_flux`].

```rust
/// Saturation of an inductor whose small-signal inductance is `L0`.
pub struct InductorSaturation {
    /// Current (A) at which the core saturates: the knee of `tanh`. A
    /// datasheet's saturation current (the current at which L has fallen
    /// 20–30 %) is roughly `0.6·i_sat` here.
    pub i_sat: f64,
    /// Inductance (H) left once the core is fully saturated, positive and
    /// at most `L0`. An air-core winding keeps about `L0/μr`.
    pub l_sat: f64,
}

impl InductorSaturation {
    /// Saturation at `i_sat` (A), keeping a tenth of `l0` (H) when
    /// saturated.
    pub fn at(i_sat: f64, l0: f64) -> Self { … }
}

/// Flux linkage (Wb) of an inductor with small-signal inductance `l0` (H)
/// carrying `i` (A).
pub fn flux(i: f64, l0: f64, s: &InductorSaturation) -> f64 { … }

/// Incremental inductance `dλ/di` (H) at current `i` (A).
pub fn incremental_inductance(i: f64, l0: f64, s: &InductorSaturation) -> f64 { … }

/// The current (A) that carries flux `lambda` (Wb): the inverse of [`flux`].
///
/// λ(i) is odd and strictly increasing (its slope is at least `l_sat`), so
/// the root is unique. Newton's method from the saturated-line estimate,
/// kept inside a shrinking bracket, finds it to a relative 1e-12 in a few
/// iterations.
pub fn current_from_flux(lambda: f64, l0: f64, s: &InductorSaturation) -> f64 { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/jfet.rs`

JFET (Junction Field-Effect Transistor) device model.

Shichman–Hodges square-law model. N-channel and P-channel are both
supported via [`JfetKind`]; the P-channel case mirrors N-channel through
sign conventions on `vgs` and `vds`.

At each Newton–Raphson iteration, [`jfet_companion`] returns a
linearised contribution that an MNA solver stamps for the [gate, drain,
source] terminals.

```rust
/// JFET channel polarity.
pub enum JfetKind {
    /// N-channel JFET (pinch-off voltage `Vp < 0`).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "nchannel"))]
    NChannel,
    /// P-channel JFET (pinch-off voltage `Vp > 0`); sign-mirrored from N-channel.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "pchannel"))]
    PChannel,
}

/// Linearised JFET companion model — the output of one Newton–Raphson
/// iteration ready for MNA stamping.
pub struct JfetCompanion {
    /// Transconductance `∂Id/∂Vgs` (S).
    pub gm: f64,
    /// Drain–source conductance `∂Id/∂Vds` (S).
    pub gds: f64,
    /// Equivalent Norton current for the MNA right-hand side (A), drain →
    /// source, in the N-channel frame (a P-channel caller negates it).
    pub i_eq: f64,
}

/// Compute JFET companion at operating point (vgs, vds).
/// Nodes order: [gate, drain, source] — same as MOSFET convention.
/// N-channel: Vp < 0 (typically -2 to -6 V), Idss > 0 (A). `vgs`, `vds` and
/// `vp` are in V.
///
/// In the ohmic region `gm = 2·Idss·Vds/Vp²` keeps its sign, so it is
/// negative when the drain is below the source.
///
/// P-channel is evaluated in the mirrored N-channel frame (`-vgs`, `-vds`,
/// `-|vp|`): `gm` and `gds` carry over to the physical device unchanged, but
/// `i_eq` is the mirrored frame's, so the physical Norton current is
/// `-i_eq`.
pub fn jfet_companion(vgs: f64, vds: f64, kind: JfetKind, idss: f64, vp: f64) -> JfetCompanion { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/led.rs`

LED colour presets.

Maps common LED colours to their typical forward voltage, then derives
DiodeParams via the Shockley equation so LEDs can be stamped as nonlinear
diodes in any MNA solver.

```rust
/// Common LED colour variants.
pub enum LedColor {
    /// Red LED (~1.8 V typical forward voltage).
    Red,
    /// Green LED (~2.2 V typical forward voltage).
    Green,
    /// Blue LED (~3.2 V typical forward voltage).
    Blue,
    /// Yellow LED (~2.0 V typical forward voltage).
    Yellow,
    /// White LED (~3.0 V typical forward voltage).
    White,
}

impl LedColor {
    /// Typical forward voltage (V) at 20 mA for this colour.
    pub fn forward_voltage(self) -> f64 { … }

    /// Parse from a lowercase string. Unknown strings default to `Red`.
    pub fn from_str(s: &str) -> Self { … }
}

/// `DiodeParams` for a given LED colour.
pub fn led_params(color: LedColor) -> DiodeParams { … }

/// `DiodeParams` from a colour name string. Unknown strings default to red.
pub fn led_params_from_str(color: &str) -> DiodeParams { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/lib.rs`

Pure-Rust electronics device physics: linearised companion models for
semiconductor and passive components used by MNA-based circuit simulators.

`sindr-devices` provides the small-signal linearisation that
Newton–Raphson solvers need at every iteration: given an applied voltage,
each device returns a `(g_eq, i_eq)` pair — an equivalent conductance and
Norton-current source. Stamp those into the MNA matrix and the solver
converges on the operating point.

This crate has **no dependency** on a particular solver. Use it standalone
if you're building your own MNA implementation, or pair it with the
companion crate [`sindr`](https://crates.io/crates/sindr) for an
end-to-end simulator.

### Devices

| Module | Device | Model |
|---|---|---|
| [`battery`] | Battery | Open-circuit voltage by state of charge, series R, optional RC pair |
| [`diode`] | Silicon diode | Shockley with series resistance, temperature IS scaling, breakdown and junction charge |
| [`bjt`] | BJT (NPN/PNP) | Ebers–Moll with Early voltage |
| [`mosfet`] | MOSFET (NMOS/PMOS) | Level-1 |
| [`jfet`] | JFET (N/P-channel) | Shichman–Hodges |
| [`igbt`] | IGBT | MOSFET gate control + BJT output conductance |
| [`led`] | LED | Diode with colour-dependent forward voltage |
| [`zener`] | Zener diode | Shockley + piecewise `1/rz` reverse-breakdown branch (sindr itself stamps a zener as a [`diode`] with `Breakdown`) |
| [`schottky`] | Schottky diode | Shockley with low-N, low-IS parameters |
| [`varactor`] | Varactor | Voltage-dependent junction capacitance |
| [`inductor`] | Saturating inductor core | `λ(i) = L_sat·i + (L₀ − L_sat)·I_sat·tanh(i/I_sat)` |
| [`thermistor`] | NTC thermistor | Beta model `R(T) = R₀·exp(β·(1/T − 1/T₀))` |
| [`photodiode`] | Photodiode | Diode + photocurrent offset |
| [`photoresistor`] | Photoresistor (LDR) | Light-level-dependent resistance |

### Quick example

```
use sindr_devices::diode::{DiodeParams, diode_companion};

let params = DiodeParams::silicon();          // IS=1e-14, N=1.0, rs=0.0
let v_applied = 0.65;                          // forward bias, volts
let (g_eq, i_eq) = diode_companion(v_applied, &params);

// Stamp g_eq into Y(p,p), Y(q,q), -g_eq into Y(p,q)/Y(q,p),
// and i_eq into b(p)/-i_eq into b(q) in your MNA system.
assert!(g_eq > 0.0);
```

### Conventions

- **Voltages and currents** are in SI units (V, A).
- **Temperature** is in kelvin. Default is 300.15 K (≈ 27 °C, the SPICE
  default). A junction's `vt()` is the thermal voltage kT/q at its own
  `temperature` ([`diode::thermal_voltage`]); its `is` is used as given,
  so scale it with [`diode::temperature_scale_is`] away from
  [`diode::T_NOM`].
- **Sign convention** for two-terminal companions: `v_applied` is the
  voltage from `nodes[0]` to `nodes[1]`, and `i_eq` is the current
  flowing into `nodes[0]`.
- **Companion form**: each `*_companion` function returns the linearised
  `(g_eq, i_eq)` at the operating point — the form Newton–Raphson stamps
  directly.

```rust
pub mod battery;

pub mod bjt;

pub mod diode;
