pub mod igbt;

pub mod inductor;

pub mod jfet;

pub mod led;

pub mod mosfet;

pub mod photodiode;

pub mod photoresistor;

pub mod regulator;

pub mod schottky;

pub mod thermistor;

pub mod varactor;

pub mod zener;
```

## `sindr-devices/src/mosfet.rs`

MOSFET Level 1 (Shichman-Hodges) model with body effect.

Implements NMOS and PMOS transistors with three operating regions:
cutoff, triode (linear), and saturation. The companion model linearizes
the device at each NR iteration for MNA stamping.

`sindr` treats every MOSFET as a three-terminal part with its body tied
to its source (Vbs = 0), so the body effect never applies there; the
model keeps it for callers that drive the body separately.

```rust
/// MOSFET type (NMOS or PMOS).
pub enum MosfetKind {
    /// N-channel MOSFET (electrons are majority carriers in the channel).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "nmos"))]
    Nmos,
    /// P-channel MOSFET (holes are majority carriers in the channel).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "pmos"))]
    Pmos,
}

impl MosfetKind {
    /// Gate–source and drain–source voltages `(vgs, vds)` of a three-terminal
    /// MOSFET with node voltages `vg`, `vd`, `vs`, in the N-channel frame that
    /// [`mosfet_companion`] works in: mirrored (`vsg`, `vsd`) for a PMOS.
    ///
    /// A three-terminal MOSFET is a discrete part, whose body is tied to its
    /// source inside the package, so its `vbs` is always 0.
    pub fn nmos_frame(self, vg: f64, vd: f64, vs: f64) -> (f64, f64) { … }
}

/// Operating region of a MOSFET.
pub enum MosfetRegion {
    /// Below threshold — channel off, negligible drain current.
    Cutoff,
    /// Triode (linear) region — `Vds` below saturation, device acts as a voltage-controlled resistor.
    Triode,
    /// Saturation region — channel pinched off, drain current set by `Vgs`.
    Saturation,
}

impl MosfetRegion {
    /// Lowercase string label for the region (`"cutoff"`, `"triode"`, `"saturation"`).
    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str { … }
}

/// MOSFET device parameters (Level 1 Shichman-Hodges).
pub struct MosfetParams {
    /// Transconductance parameter (A/V^2). SPICE KP parameter.
    pub kp: f64,
    /// Zero-bias threshold voltage (V). SPICE VTO parameter, signed as in
    /// SPICE: positive for an enhancement NMOS, negative for an enhancement
    /// PMOS (see [`MosfetParams::in_nmos_frame`]).
    pub vto: f64,
    /// Channel-length modulation (1/V). SPICE LAMBDA parameter.
    pub lambda: f64,
    /// Body effect coefficient (V^0.5). SPICE GAMMA parameter.
    pub gamma: f64,
    /// Surface potential (V). SPICE PHI parameter.
    pub phi: f64,
    /// Flicker-noise coefficient. Noise analysis puts `KF·|Id|^AF / f`
    /// (A²/Hz) across drain–source. sindr has no channel geometry, so this
    /// is SPICE's `KF/(Cox·L²)`. Default 0: no flicker noise.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub kf: f64,
    /// Flicker-noise current exponent AF. Default 1.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_af"))]
    pub af: f64,
}

impl MosfetParams {
    /// Default NMOS parameters (typical educational values).
    pub fn default_nmos() -> Self { … }

    /// Default PMOS parameters (typical educational values).
    pub fn default_pmos() -> Self { … }

    /// These parameters in the N-channel frame that [`mosfet_companion`]
    /// works in. Callers mirror a PMOS's voltages (`vsg`, `vsd`, …) before
    /// calling it; this mirrors the threshold to match, so a SPICE-signed
    /// VTO (−0.7 V for [`MosfetParams::default_pmos`]) becomes the +0.7 V
    /// the N-channel equations expect.
    pub fn in_nmos_frame(&self, kind: MosfetKind) -> MosfetParams { … }
}

/// Companion model output for MNA stamping.
pub struct MosfetCompanion {
    /// Drain current at the operating point (A), drain → source, in the
    /// NMOS frame: callers mirror a PMOS (negate) to get its physical current.
    pub id: f64,
    /// Transconductance ∂Id/∂Vgs (S).
    pub gm: f64,
    /// Output conductance ∂Id/∂Vds (S).
    pub gds: f64,
    /// Body transconductance ∂Id/∂Vbs (S), from the body effect. Zero when
    /// Vbs >= PHI, where the threshold stops depending on Vbs.
    pub gmb: f64,
    /// Operating region.
    pub region: MosfetRegion,
    /// Effective threshold voltage after the body effect (V), NMOS frame.
    pub vth: f64,
}

/// Compute threshold voltage with body effect.
///
/// Vth = VTO + GAMMA * (sqrt(PHI - Vbs) - sqrt(PHI))
///
/// For NMOS with Vbs <= 0: Vth increases (harder to turn on). Once the body
/// is forward-biased past PHI (Vbs >= PHI) the sqrt term is clamped to 0
/// and Vth no longer depends on Vbs.
/// For PMOS, caller passes sign-adjusted Vbs and
/// [`MosfetParams::in_nmos_frame`] parameters. With the body tied to the
/// source, as in sindr, Vbs = 0 and Vth = VTO.
pub fn threshold_voltage(vbs: f64, params: &MosfetParams) -> f64 { … }

/// Evaluate the Level 1 MOSFET model at a given operating point.
///
/// Works in the N-channel frame. For NMOS: Vgs, Vds, Vbs are used directly.
/// For PMOS: pass the mirrored voltages (Vsg, Vsd, Vsb; see
/// [`MosfetKind::nmos_frame`]) and [`MosfetParams::in_nmos_frame`]
/// parameters, so the equations work identically.
///
/// `gmb` is zero once the body is forward-biased past PHI, matching
/// [`threshold_voltage`].
pub fn mosfet_companion(vgs: f64, vds: f64, vbs: f64, params: &MosfetParams) -> MosfetCompanion { … }

/// Detect MOSFET operating region from terminal voltages.
pub fn detect_region(vgs: f64, vds: f64, vth: f64) -> MosfetRegion { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/photodiode.rs`

Photodiode companion model.

Model: I = IS*(exp(Vd/(N*VT))-1) - I_photo, with VT = kT/q at the
junction `temperature`
I_photo = responsivity * irradiance (photocurrent, flows in reverse direction)

In dark (irradiance=0), behaves identically to a silicon diode.
With irradiance, produces reverse photocurrent that can drive loads.

```rust
/// Photodiode parameters.
pub struct PhotodiodeParams {
    /// Dark saturation current (A).
    pub is: f64,
    /// Ideality factor (~1.0 for photodiodes).
    pub n: f64,
    /// Responsivity (A/W). Converts irradiance to photocurrent.
    /// Typical silicon photodiode: 0.4–0.7 A/W.
    pub responsivity: f64,
    /// Junction temperature (K). Default 300.15 K = 27°C. Sets the thermal
    /// voltage [`PhotodiodeParams::vt`]; `is` is used as given.
    pub temperature: f64,
}

impl PhotodiodeParams {
    /// Silicon photodiode: IS = 1e-12 A, N = 1.0, responsivity = 0.5 A/W.
    pub fn silicon() -> Self { … }

    /// Thermal voltage kT/q (V) at the junction temperature.
    pub fn vt(&self) -> f64 { … }
}

/// Linearized companion model for a photodiode at operating point v_d.
///
/// Returns `(g_d, i_eq)`: conductance (S) and Norton current (A) for current
/// flowing anode → cathode, at `v_d` = anode − cathode (V). `irradiance` is
/// incident optical power in W (not W/m²). `i_eq` includes the
/// photocurrent, which flows cathode → anode, opposite to forward current.
pub fn photodiode_companion(v_d: f64, irradiance: f64, params: &PhotodiodeParams) -> (f64, f64) { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/photoresistor.rs`

Photoresistor (LDR) model: resistance as a function of illuminance.

Uses logarithmic interpolation between dark and bright endpoints,
matching real LDR behaviour (resistance halves roughly every decade of lux).

```rust
/// Photoresistor parameters.
pub struct PhotoresistorParams {
    /// Resistance in darkness (Ω). Default: 1 MΩ.
    pub r_dark: f64,
    /// Resistance at full illumination (Ω). Default: 1 kΩ.
    pub r_bright: f64,
}

/// Compute LDR resistance from a normalised light level.
///
/// `light_level` is clamped to `[0.0, 1.0]`:
/// - `0.0` → `params.r_dark`
/// - `1.0` → `params.r_bright`
///
/// Interpolation is logarithmic: `R = r_dark * (r_bright / r_dark) ^ light_level`
pub fn ldr_resistance(light_level: f64, params: &PhotoresistorParams) -> f64 { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/regulator.rs`

Linear voltage regulator: dropout, quiescent current, current limit,
line and load regulation.

The output is a piecewise-linear function of the input voltage and the
output current, both measured from the regulator's ground pin:

```text
regulating: Vout = V + line·(Vin − (V + Vdo)) − Rout·Iout
dropout:    Vout = Vin − Vdo − Rdo·Iout
```

whichever is lower. Past the current limit the output falls steeply, so
the current stays within 1 % of the limit into any load, short circuits
included. The input draws `Iout + Iq`.

```rust
/// Regulator parameters. [`Default`] is ideal: no dropout, no quiescent
/// current, no limit, perfect regulation, but never more out than in.
pub struct RegulatorParams {
    /// Dropout voltage at no load (V): the least `Vin − Vout` it regulates
    /// with.
    pub dropout: f64,
    /// Rise in dropout per ampere of output current (Ω), for a dropout that
    /// grows with load.
    pub dropout_resistance: f64,
    /// Quiescent (ground-pin) current (A), drawn from the input on top of
    /// the output current.
    pub quiescent_current: f64,
    /// Output current limit (A). `None` is unlimited.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub current_limit: Option<f64>,
    /// Line regulation: change in output per volt of input (V/V), around
    /// the input where it just leaves dropout.
    pub line_regulation: f64,
    /// Load regulation as an output resistance (Ω): the output falls this
    /// much per ampere drawn.
    pub output_resistance: f64,
}

impl RegulatorParams {
    /// An LM7805-class 5 V regulator, from the ST L78 and Fairchild LM78xx
    /// datasheets at 25 °C: 2 V dropout (typical, 1 A), 4.3 mA quiescent
    /// (typical), 2.2 A peak current, line regulation 3 mV over 7–25 V
    /// (typical), load regulation 100 mV over 5 mA–1.5 A (maximum; no
    /// typical is given). Short-circuit foldback (0.23 A at 35 V in) is not
    /// modelled.
    pub fn lm7805() -> Self { … }

    /// An AMS1117-class low-dropout regulator, from its datasheet: 1.1 V
    /// dropout at 0.8 A (typical), 5 mA quiescent (typical), 1.1 A current
    /// limit (typical), line regulation 0.2 % and load regulation 0.4 %
    /// (maxima) of a 3.3 V output, over 4.75–12 V in and 0–0.8 A out.
    pub fn ams1117() -> Self { … }
}

/// Which part of its characteristic a regulator is on.
pub enum RegulatorRegion {
    /// Holding its set voltage (less line and load regulation).
    Regulating,
    /// Out of headroom: the output follows the input down.
    Dropout,
}

/// The regulator's output on one linear piece:
/// `Vout = offset + d_vin·Vin + d_iout·Iout`, all from the ground pin.
pub struct RegulatorLinear {
    /// Constant term (V).
    pub offset: f64,
    /// ∂Vout/∂Vin (V/V).
    pub d_vin: f64,
    /// ∂Vout/∂Iout (Ω), negative.
    pub d_iout: f64,
    /// Regulating or in dropout.
    pub region: RegulatorRegion,
    /// `true` when past the current limit.
    pub limiting: bool,
}

impl RegulatorLinear {
    /// The output voltage this piece gives at `vin`, `iout`.
    pub fn vout(&self, vin: f64, iout: f64) -> f64 { … }
}

/// The piece of a regulator set to `voltage` that applies at input `vin`
/// (V, from the ground pin) and output current `iout` (A, out of the output
/// pin).
pub fn regulator_piece(
    params: &RegulatorParams,
    voltage: f64,
    vin: f64,
    iout: f64,
) -> RegulatorLinear { … }

/// Power the regulator dissipates (W): `(Vin − Vout)·Iout + Vin·Iq`, with
/// voltages from the ground pin.
pub fn regulator_dissipation(params: &RegulatorParams, vin: f64, vout: f64, iout: f64) -> f64 { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/schottky.rs`

Schottky diode companion model.

Schottky diodes use the same Shockley equation as silicon diodes
but with higher saturation current (IS ≈ 1e-8 A) and lower forward
voltage (~0.3V vs ~0.6V silicon). Reuses diode_companion().

```rust
/// Schottky diode parameters.
pub struct SchottkyParams {
    /// Saturation current (A). Higher than silicon due to lower barrier.
    pub is: f64,
    /// Emission coefficient (dimensionless). ~1.0 for Schottky (more ideal
    /// than silicon).
    pub n: f64,
}

impl SchottkyParams {
    /// Standard BAT85 Schottky: IS = 1e-8 A, N = 1.0 → Vf ≈ 0.3V at 10 mA.
    pub fn standard() -> Self { … }
}

/// Linearized companion model for a Schottky diode at operating point v_d.
///
/// Returns `(g_d, i_eq)`: conductance (S) and equivalent Norton current (A)
/// for current flowing anode → cathode, at `v_d` = anode − cathode (V).
/// Delegates to diode_companion with Schottky parameters.
pub fn schottky_companion(v_d: f64, params: &SchottkyParams) -> (f64, f64) { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/thermistor.rs`

NTC thermistor resistance model (Beta model).

Thermistors have temperature-dependent resistance but are passive —
resistance is computed once from the temperature parameter, not from
circuit voltages. No NR iteration needed.

```rust
/// NTC thermistor parameters (Beta model).
pub struct ThermistorParams {
    /// Resistance at reference temperature T0 (Ω).
    pub r0: f64,
    /// Beta coefficient (K). Typically 3000–5000 for NTC.
    pub beta: f64,
    /// Reference temperature (K). Standard: 298.15 K (25°C).
    pub t0: f64,
}

impl ThermistorParams {
    /// Standard 10 kΩ NTC thermistor (Epcos B57164K0103K000 or equivalent).
    /// R0 = 10kΩ at 25°C, Beta = 3950 K.
    pub fn ntc_10k() -> Self { … }
}

/// Compute thermistor resistance at a given temperature (Kelvin).
///
/// Uses the Beta model: R(T) = R0 * exp(beta * (1/T - 1/T0))
///
/// Does not panic; clamps T to a minimum of 1 K to avoid division by zero.
pub fn thermistor_resistance(temperature_k: f64, params: &ThermistorParams) -> f64 { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/varactor.rs`

Varactor diode model: voltage-dependent junction capacitance.

A varactor is a reverse-biased diode whose junction capacitance varies with
applied voltage. In DC analysis it is an open circuit. In transient analysis
the capacitance is evaluated at the previous timestep voltage (freeze-and-stamp).
In AC analysis it is the capacitance at the DC bias point.

```rust
/// Varactor diode parameters.
pub struct VaractorParams {
    /// Zero-bias junction capacitance (F). Typical: 10e-12 (10 pF).
    pub cj0: f64,
    /// Built-in junction potential (V). Typical: 0.7 for Si.
    pub phi: f64,
    /// Grading coefficient (dimensionless). Typical: 0.5 (abrupt junction).
    pub m: f64,
}

/// Junction capacitance (F) at `v` = anode − cathode (V); reverse bias is
/// negative.
///
/// C_j(V) = C_j0 / (1 - V/phi)^m
///
/// Clamped: V must not reach phi (singularity). Clamp V to 0.9 * phi max.
/// For reverse bias (V < 0), capacitance increases correctly.
/// For forward bias (V approaching phi), capacitance would diverge — clamp.
pub fn junction_capacitance(v: f64, params: &VaractorParams) -> f64 { … }

/// Compute the transient companion model for the varactor at `v_prev`
/// (V, anode − cathode) over a step of `dt` seconds.
///
/// Returns `(g_eq, i_eq)`, in S and A, where:
/// - g_eq = C_j(v_prev) / dt  (backward Euler capacitor conductance)
/// - i_eq = -g_eq * v_prev    (capacitor history current)
///
/// The current from anode to cathode is `g_eq * v + i_eq`, the same
/// convention as [`diode_companion`](crate::diode::diode_companion).
///
/// In DC analysis, stamp as open circuit: return (0.0, 0.0).
/// Caller passes dt = 0.0 to signal DC, returning open circuit.
pub fn varactor_companion(v_prev: f64, dt: f64, params: &VaractorParams) -> (f64, f64) { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/zener.rs`

Zener diode model: piecewise companion for Newton-Raphson simulation.

Forward bias: standard Shockley diode.
Reverse breakdown: linearised clamp at -Vz.

```rust
/// Zener diode parameters.
pub struct ZenerParams {
    /// Breakdown voltage (V), positive: 5.1 for a BZX55C5V1.
    pub vz: f64,
    /// Breakdown region dynamic resistance (Ω). Smaller = sharper knee.
    pub rz: f64,
    /// Saturation current for the forward diode region (A).
    pub is: f64,
    /// Junction temperature (K). Default 300.15 K = 27°C. Sets the thermal
    /// voltage [`ZenerParams::vt`]; `is` is used as given.
    pub temperature: f64,
}

impl ZenerParams {
    /// Construct default Zener parameters for the given breakdown voltage `vz` (V).
    pub fn new(vz: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// Thermal voltage kT/q (V) at the junction temperature.
    pub fn vt(&self) -> f64 { … }
}

/// Piecewise Zener companion model. Returns `(g_eq, i_eq)` for MNA stamping:
/// `g_eq` in S and `i_eq` in A, for current flowing anode → cathode, at
/// `v_d` = anode − cathode (V). Breakdown is `v_d ≤ −vz`.
///
/// - `v_d > -vz`: standard Shockley companion (clamped to avoid overflow).
/// - `v_d <= -vz`: linearised 1/rz clamp driving the junction to -Vz.
pub fn zener_companion(v_d: f64, params: &ZenerParams) -> (f64, f64) { … }
```


# Examples

## `sindr/examples/bjt_amplifier.rs`

```rust
use sindr::{examples, solve_circuit};

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let circuit = examples::npn_common_emitter();
    let result = solve_circuit(&circuit)?;

    let bjt = result
        .bjt_results
        .first()
        .ok_or("expected at least one BJT in the result")?;

    println!("=== NPN Common Emitter Operating Point ===");
    println!("Vbe    = {:.4} V", bjt.vbe);
    println!("Vce    = {:.4} V", bjt.vce);
    println!("Ib     = {:.4} mA", bjt.ib * 1e3);
    println!("Ic     = {:.4} mA", bjt.ic * 1e3);
    println!("Ie     = {:.4} mA", bjt.ie * 1e3);
    println!("Region : {}", bjt.region);
    println!("Power  = {:.4} mW", bjt.power * 1e3);

    Ok(())
}
```

## `sindr/examples/bode_plot.rs`

```rust
use sindr::ac_analysis::{solve_ac, AcConfig, FrequencySpacing};
use sindr::examples;

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let circuit = examples::rc_lowpass_filter();

    let config = AcConfig {
        f_start: 10.0,
        f_stop: 100_000.0,
        num_points: 50,
        spacing: FrequencySpacing::Logarithmic,
        source_id: "V1".into(),
        ac_magnitude: 1.0,
    };

    let result = solve_ac(&circuit, &config)?;

    println!("=== RC Low-Pass Filter — Bode Plot ===");
    println!("{:>10}\t{:>7}\t{:>7}", "freq(Hz)", "gain(dB)", "phase(deg)");

    for point in result.points.iter() {
        let gain = point.gain_db("n2", config.ac_magnitude).unwrap_or(f64::NAN);
        let phase = point.phase_deg("n2").unwrap_or(f64::NAN);
        println!("{:>10.2}\t{:>7.2}\t{:>7.2}", point.frequency, gain, phase);
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

## `sindr/examples/dc_sweep_diode.rs`

```rust
// DC sweep of a series-resistor + diode circuit (I-V curve)
//
// Topology: V1 (swept) → R_series (100 Ω) → D1 (diode) → GND
//
// Run: cargo run -p sindr --example dc_sweep_diode
//
// Expected output:
//   V_applied(V)    I_diode(A)
//   Reverse-bias (V < 0): near-zero current
//   Forward-bias (V > ~0.5): exponential current turn-on

use sindr::{dc_sweep, Circuit, CircuitElement};

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let circuit = Circuit {
        ground_node: "0".into(),
        components: vec![
            CircuitElement::VoltageSource {
                id: "V1".into(),
                nodes: ["n1".into(), "0".into()],
                voltage: 0.0, // initial value irrelevant; dc_sweep overrides it
                waveform: None,
            },
            // Series resistor required: diode directly across V-source is degenerate
            CircuitElement::Resistor {
                id: "R_series".into(),
                nodes: ["n1".into(), "n2".into()],
                resistance: 100.0,
            },
            CircuitElement::Diode {
                id: "D1".into(),
                nodes: ["n2".into(), "0".into()], // anode: n2, cathode: GND
                temperature: 300.15,
                model: None,
            },
        ],
        ..Default::default()
    };

    // Sweep V1 from -1 V to +1 V in 101 points
    let sweep = dc_sweep(&circuit, "V1", -1.0, 1.0, 101)?;

    println!("V_applied(V)\tI_diode(A)");
    for (v, i) in sweep.component_current_curve("D1") {
        println!("{:>8.3}\t{:>12.6e}", v, i);
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

## `sindr/examples/initial_voltages.rs`

```rust
// Seeding the Newton–Raphson starting point (SPICE `.nodeset`)
//
// Topology: V1 (5 V) → R1 (1 kΩ) → D1 → D2 → GND (two diodes in series)
//
// Run: cargo run -p sindr --example initial_voltages
//
// Expected output: both solves land on the same operating point
// (~1.38 V across the pair); the seed only changes where Newton starts.
// Seeds apply to nonlinear DC only, and node names that don't exist are
// ignored.

use std::collections::HashMap;

use sindr::{solve_circuit, solve_circuit_with_initial_voltages, Circuit, CircuitElement};

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let circuit = Circuit {
        ground_node: "0".into(),
        components: vec![
            CircuitElement::VoltageSource {
                id: "V1".into(),
                nodes: ["in".into(), "0".into()],
                voltage: 5.0,
                waveform: None,
            },
            CircuitElement::Resistor {
                id: "R1".into(),
                nodes: ["in".into(), "top".into()],
                resistance: 1_000.0,
            },
            CircuitElement::Diode {
                id: "D1".into(),
                nodes: ["top".into(), "mid".into()],
                temperature: 300.15,
                model: None,
            },
            CircuitElement::Diode {
                id: "D2".into(),
                nodes: ["mid".into(), "0".into()],
                temperature: 300.15,
                model: None,
            },
        ],
        ..Default::default()
    };

    let plain = solve_circuit(&circuit)?;

    // Start Newton near the expected answer: ~0.65 V per diode.
    let seed = HashMap::from([("top".to_string(), 1.3), ("mid".to_string(), 0.65)]);
    let seeded = solve_circuit_with_initial_voltages(&circuit, &seed)?;

    for node in ["top", "mid"] {
        println!(
            "V({node}): plain {:.6} V, seeded {:.6} V",
            plain.node_voltages[node], seeded.node_voltages[node]
        );
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

## `sindr/examples/parse_netlist.rs`

```rust
//! Parse a SPICE3 netlist and solve it.
//!
//! Run with the `spice` feature enabled:
//!
//! ```text
//! cargo run --example parse_netlist --features spice
//! ```
//!
//! Demonstrates the full `sindr::spice` flow: parse a deck into a
//! `Circuit`, dispatch the deck's analysis directives to the matching
//! solver routine, and render a parse error with miette's fancy reporter.

use sindr::spice::{parse_str, parse_str_with_options, AnalysisRequest, ParseOptions};

// A resistor divider plus `.dc` sweep, `.tf` and `.sens` directives. V1 = 9 V across
// R1 = 1k / R2 = 2k, so node `n2` sits at 6 V at the nominal source value.
const DECK: &str = "* resistor divider\n\
                    V1 n1 0 DC 9\n\
                    R1 n1 n2 1k\n\
                    R2 n2 0 2k\n\
                    .dc V1 0 9 0.9\n\
                    .tf V(n2) V1\n\
                    .sens V(n2)\n\
                    .end\n";

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    // 1. Parse (strict mode). The result is a plain `sindr::Circuit`
    //    plus the deck's analysis directives.
    let netlist = parse_str(DECK)?;
    println!(
        "parsed `{}` — {} components, {} analyses",
        netlist.title,
        netlist.circuit.components.len(),
        netlist.analyses.len()
    );

    // 2. Solve the operating point directly.
    let op = sindr::solve_circuit(&netlist.circuit)?;
    println!("V(n2) = {:.3} V", op.node_voltages["n2"]);

    // 3. Dispatch each parsed directive to the matching sindr routine.
    for analysis in &netlist.analyses {
        match analysis {
            AnalysisRequest::Op => {
                sindr::solve_circuit(&netlist.circuit)?;
            }
            AnalysisRequest::Dc { source, .. } => {
                let (axis, _outer) = analysis.dc_axes().ok_or("not a .dc")??;
                let sweep = sindr::dc_sweep(
                    &netlist.circuit,
                    &axis.source_id,
                    axis.start,
                    axis.stop,
                    axis.num_points,
                )?;
                let curve = sweep.node_voltage_curve("n2");
                println!(
                    "dc sweep of {source}: {} points, V(n2) {:.3}..{:.3} V",
                    curve.len(),
                    curve.first().map(|p| p.1).unwrap_or(0.0),
                    curve.last().map(|p| p.1).unwrap_or(0.0),
                );
            }
            AnalysisRequest::Tran { tstop, tstep, .. } => {
                let config = analysis.transient_config().ok_or("not a .tran")?;
                let result = sindr::solve_transient(&netlist.circuit, &config)?;
                let steps = result.transient.map_or(0, |t| t.timesteps.len());
                println!("transient to {tstop} s in {tstep} s steps: {steps} snapshots");
            }
            AnalysisRequest::Ac { fstart, fstop, .. } => {
                println!("ac sweep {fstart}..{fstop} Hz (build an AcConfig for solve_ac)");
            }
            AnalysisRequest::Sens { .. } => {
                let config = analysis.sens_config().ok_or("not a .sens")?;
                let sens = sindr::solve_sensitivity(&netlist.circuit, &config)?;
                println!("sens: {} parameters", sens.entries.len());
            }
            AnalysisRequest::Noise { .. } => {
                let config = analysis.noise_config().ok_or("not a .noise")?;
                let noise = sindr::solve_noise(&netlist.circuit, &config)?;
                println!("noise: {} points", noise.points.len());
            }
            AnalysisRequest::Tf { .. } => {
                let config = analysis.tf_config().ok_or("not a .tf")?;
                let tf = sindr::solve_tf(&netlist.circuit, &config)?;
                println!(
                    "tf: gain {:.4}, input {:.1} Ω, output {:.1} Ω",
                    tf.gain, tf.input_resistance, tf.output_resistance
                );
            }
        }
    }

    // 4. Lenient mode: an unsupported element (M = MOSFET) becomes a
    //    collected warning instead of a hard error.
    let with_mosfet = format!("{DECK}M1 n2 n1 0 nmod\n");
    let opts = ParseOptions {
        strict: false,
        include_search_path: None,
    };
    let lenient = parse_str_with_options(&with_mosfet, opts)?;
    for warning in &lenient.warnings {
        println!("warning: {warning:?}");
    }

    // 5. Strict mode on a bad deck: render the diagnostic with miette's
    //    fancy reporter for an annotated, underlined span.
    if let Err(e) = parse_str("* bad\nZ1 a b 1\n.end\n") {
        eprintln!("{:?}", miette::Report::new(e));
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

## `sindr/examples/run_example.rs`

```rust
use std::env;

use sindr::{get_examples, solve_circuit};

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let id = env::args().nth(1).ok_or(
        "usage: cargo run --example run_example -- <id>\n\
         (run `cargo run --example list_examples` to see available ids)",
    )?;

    let example = get_examples()
        .into_iter()
        .find(|ex| ex.id == id)
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("no example with id '{id}'"))?;

    println!("=== {} ===", example.name);
    println!("{}\n", example.description);

    let result = solve_circuit(&example.circuit)?;

    let mut nodes: Vec<_> = result.node_voltages.iter().collect();
    nodes.sort_by_key(|(k, _)| (*k).clone());
    println!("Node voltages:");
    for (node, v) in nodes {
        println!("  {:<10} = {:>10.4} V", node, v);
    }

    if !result.bjt_results.is_empty() {
        println!("\nBJT operating points:");
        for bjt in &result.bjt_results {
            println!(
                "  {:<6} Vbe={:.3}V Vce={:.3}V Ic={:.3}mA region={}",
                bjt.id,
                bjt.vbe,
                bjt.vce,
                bjt.ic * 1e3,
                bjt.region
            );
        }
    }

    if let Some(transient) = result.transient {
        let n = transient.timesteps.len();
        if n > 0 {
            let first = &transient.timesteps[0];
            let last = &transient.timesteps[n - 1];
            println!(
                "\nTransient: {n} timesteps, t = {:.6}s → {:.6}s",
                first.time, last.time
            );
        }
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

## `sindr/examples/sensitivity.rs`

```rust
use sindr::{examples, solve_sensitivity, SensConfig, TfOutput};

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let circuit = examples::npn_common_emitter();

    // Which part moves the collector voltage most?
    let config = SensConfig {
        output: TfOutput::Voltage {
            node: "collector".into(),
            reference: None,
        },
    };
    let sens = solve_sensitivity(&circuit, &config)?;

    println!("=== NPN Common Emitter — .sens V(collector) ===");
    println!("{:>6}\t{:>12}\t{:>14}", "part", "value", "dV per +1%");
    for entry in &sens.entries {
        println!(
            "{:>6}\t{:>12.1}\t{:>11.2} mV",
            entry.component_id,
            entry.value,
            entry.per_percent * 1e3
        );
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

## `sindr/examples/temperature_sweep.rs`

```rust
// Temperature sweep of a forward-biased silicon diode
//
// Topology: V1 (5 V) → R1 (1 kΩ) → D1 (diode) → GND
//
// Run: cargo run -p sindr --example temperature_sweep
//
// Expected output:
//   T(°C)    V_diode(V)
//   The forward drop falls by about 1.7 mV/K as the junction warms
//   (~0.77 V at −23 °C down to ~0.53 V at 127 °C).

use sindr::{temperature_sweep, Circuit, CircuitElement};

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let circuit = Circuit {
        ground_node: "0".into(),
        components: vec![
            CircuitElement::VoltageSource {
                id: "V1".into(),
                nodes: ["in".into(), "0".into()],
                voltage: 5.0,
                waveform: None,
            },
            CircuitElement::Resistor {
                id: "R1".into(),
                nodes: ["in".into(), "out".into()],
                resistance: 1_000.0,
            },
            CircuitElement::Diode {
                id: "D1".into(),
                nodes: ["out".into(), "0".into()],
                temperature: 300.15, // overridden at each sweep point
                model: None,
            },
        ],
        ..Default::default()
    };

    // 250 K to 400 K (−23 °C to 127 °C) in 7 points
    let sweep = temperature_sweep(&circuit, 250.0, 400.0, 7)?;

    println!("T(°C)\tV_diode(V)");
    for point in &sweep.points {
        println!(
            "{:>6.1}\t{:.4}",
            point.temperature_kelvin - 273.15,
            point.result.node_voltages["out"]
        );
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

## `sindr/examples/transfer_function.rs`

```rust
use sindr::{examples, solve_tf, TfConfig, TfOutput};

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let circuit = examples::npn_common_emitter();

    // How much supply ripple reaches the collector, what the supply sees,
    // and how stiff the collector node is.
    let config = TfConfig {
        output: TfOutput::Voltage {
            node: "collector".into(),
            reference: None,
        },
        input_source: "Vcc".into(),
    };
    let tf = solve_tf(&circuit, &config)?;

    println!("=== NPN Common Emitter — .tf V(collector) Vcc ===");
    println!("gain               = {:.4} V/V", tf.gain);
    println!("input resistance   = {:.1} Ω", tf.input_resistance);
    println!("output resistance  = {:.1} Ω", tf.output_resistance);

    Ok(())
}
```

## `sindr/examples/transient_rc.rs`

```rust
use sindr::{examples, solve_circuit};

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let circuit = examples::rc_lowpass_filter();
    let result = solve_circuit(&circuit)?;
    let transient = result
        .transient
        .ok_or("expected transient data — circuit should contain a capacitor")?;

    println!("=== RC Low-Pass Filter — Step Response ===");
    println!("time(s)\t\tV_out(V)");

    let steps = &transient.timesteps;
    let stride = (steps.len() / 25).max(1);
    for (i, snap) in steps.iter().enumerate() {
        if i % stride == 0 {
            let v_out = snap.node_voltages.get("n2").copied().unwrap_or(0.0);
            println!("{:.6}\t{:.4}", snap.time, v_out);
        }
    }
    if let Some(last) = steps.last() {
        let v_out = last.node_voltages.get("n2").copied().unwrap_or(0.0);
        println!("{:.6}\t{:.4}", last.time, v_out);
    }

    Ok(())
}
```
